episodes.title: Assault on Bill Barker at Selma
episodes.summary: Six young white men struck Bill Barker, a Black man, over the head, robbed him and threw him into the flooded river at Selma after a dice game. One man allegedly came at him with a razor. Four suspects were arrested and released.

episodes.title: Lynching of John Hollins
episodes.summary: A mob of masked men took John Hollins, a Negro, off a train near Drew, Miss., and shot him to death. He was charged with attempting to assault a white girl. Date not given in the article.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Archie Hill
episodes.summary: After a Negro named Hill shot a streetcar conductor in Pasadena, an attempt was made to lynch him; he was safely lodged in the Los Angeles county jail. The text gives no further detail on the attempt.

episodes.title: Logansport manhunt
episodes.summary: Threshers pursued an unknown Negro man for several miles after he allegedly tried to assault a farmer's wife near Logansport, firing several shots at him. He escaped into a swamp, believed badly wounded. Farmers were arming to resume the chase at dawn, and a lynching was expected.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of William Spencer
episodes.summary: After William Spencer, a Black man, shot Charles McFarlane in the Criminal Courts building, a crowd of men shouting "Lynch him!" tried to take him from a detective. Police forced them back, and a crowd outside also called for lynching.

episodes.title: Shooting of John Taylor at Castle Haynes
episodes.summary: During a convict escape from the county camp, a guard shot dead convict Chas. Taylor, a Black man. A guard also shot Forney George, a Black convict, according to two recaptured convicts. Both are reported as shot by guards.

episodes.title: Killing of a railroad survey superintendent near Spring Hill, Louisiana
episodes.summary: Whitecaps repeatedly served notice on a surveying crew on the Louisiana and Arkansas line to discharge its Negro cooks or leave the parish. The threats were disregarded, and the superintendent was later found dead, assassinated by unknown parties.

episodes.title: Whitecap attack on the home of Eli Hilson
episodes.summary: Armed Whitecaps visited the home of Eli Hilson, a Negro in Lincoln County, Mississippi, and riddled his house with bullets. No one was killed. Certain Negroes had been ordered to leave the county.

episodes.title: Shooting of Willie Page
episodes.summary: Special policeman Jerry Lynch, employed by the Louisville & Nashville Railroad on the river front, shot into a crowd of Negro boys near noon, wounding Willie Page, 13, in the hip. The boy was treated by the city physician and sent home.

episodes.title: Lynching of Phil Davis, Walter Carter and Clint Thomas
episodes.summary: After Robert Adageer was shot at Belcher, citizens captured three Negroes near the town and hid them to prevent rescue, openly intending to lynch them. Two other suspects were pursued by posses toward Desoto parish. The fate of the captured men was unconfirmed.

episodes.title: Expulsion of Black residents from Webrum, Pennsylvania
episodes.summary: After a Black man was said to have killed a white man in Indiana, Pa. and escaped, white residents ordered the town's Negroes to leave. When they did not comply, the white residents attacked and pulled down the Negroes' shacks, and the Negroes departed.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Black prisoners at Shawnee, Oklahoma Territory
episodes.summary: Citizens aroused by an unknown man's throat-cut murder in the Shawnee stock yards planned summary vengeance on three arrested Black men. Sheriff and deputies removed the prisoners to Tecumseh before dark; no violence is reported.

episodes.title: Union gambling raid killing
episodes.summary: Police raided a gambling party of Negroes in Union, SC, and fired shots as the men tried to escape. One Negro was shot in the bowels and died; another was shot in the foot. Witnesses at the inquest said police killed him.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Andrew Gilford
episodes.summary: After Albert Kane, white, was stabbed by Andrew Gilford, colored, crowds marched around Mendota talking of lynching and gathered at the jail. Special police dispersed the mob and guarded the jail.

episodes.title: Whipping of Williams in Lee County, Georgia
episodes.summary: A committee of farmers in Lee County, below Americus, gave Negro preacher Williams a severe thrashing and advised him to leave for Columbus after he allegedly stirred Black workers to strike.

episodes.title: Shooting of Ben Douglass
episodes.summary: Officers Huffman and Richardson answered a disturbance at Negro quarters on Upper Front street and tried to arrest Ben Douglass; Deputy Richardson shot him through the shoulder. Douglass was not known to be armed. The physician says the wound will not be fatal.

episodes.title: Lynching of David Wyatt
episodes.summary: A mob lynched David J. Wyatt, an Afro-American, at Belleville, Illinois, after his arrest following a shooting. Black citizens held a mass meeting, adopted resolutions demanding prosecution of the mob, and formed a committee to visit state officers and a fund for Wyatt's family.

episodes.title: Expulsion of Black railroad workers near Pennington Gap, Virginia
episodes.summary: An armed mob of white men from Harlan County, Ky., entered a Louisville and Nashville railroad camp near Pennington Gap, Lee County, Va., demanded the contractors discharge about 100 Negro workers, and ordered them to leave work and the county. The camp was emptied and work suspended.

episodes.title: Beating of Arthur Patterson and William Black
episodes.summary: A mob of about five hundred white men set upon Arthur Patterson and Wm. Black, colored, suspected of shooting Jeremiah Healy, and beat them so badly they had to be taken to the hospital. Police arrived and stopped the killing.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of two Black men in Pike County, Missouri (1903)
episodes.summary: A large crowd gathered to hang two young Black men accused of attempted assault on a white woman; constable May moved them to the Bowling Green jail. A second mob came to the jail at night, and Sheriff Lindsey, his family and armed threats turned it back. The men were later taken to Troy.

episodes.title: Expulsion of Black waiters from Linton, Indiana
episodes.summary: A crowd of several thousand miners gathered outside the Elks banquet hall at Linton, threatened to dynamite the building unless the eight Terre Haute Black cooks and waiters were sent out of town, and the men were hurried by cab to Jasonville and put on a train to Terre Haute.

episodes.title: Clarksville circus tent shooting
episodes.summary: A drunken Black man attacked a deputy sheriff during a circus at Clarksville, Texas, and was shot to death before a large crowd. The date is not given beyond the issue date.

episodes.title: Whipping of Henry Carr
episodes.summary: Henry Carr, a Black storekeeper in Alexandria, La., was given fifty lashes with a rawhide by leading white citizens, who then ordered him to leave the town and the state. The paper links it to Carr making J. C. Mosley apologize to his wife.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Everidge Williams and Walter Brown
episodes.doubt: the War Department disputed that soldiers attempted a lynching
episodes.summary: Soldiers from Fort Leavenworth and citizens, about twenty-five strong, surrounded the homes of Negroes Everidge Williams and Walter Brown intending to lynch them. Police with rifles and revolvers got the men away to the police station.

episodes.title: Cooper whippings
episodes.summary: In Cooper, Delta county, Texas, the Regulars took out negro loafers, sneak thieves and petty criminals, whipped them and ordered them to leave town. The report is dated New Orleans, June 26, and gives no exact date for the whipping.

episodes.title: Banishment of Aaron P. Prioleau from Eutawville
episodes.summary: Prioleau says that about April 1 or 8, 1903, he was forced to leave Eutawville to escape lynching after a pretended arrest, and that he is now threatened with being shot if seen there and his property is taken by force.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Louis Everson
episodes.summary: Farmers gathered in Lawrenceburg and other county towns and openly threatened lynching of a negro held at the jail on suspicion of the Kaiser murder. Sheriff's deputies guarded the jail; the crowd dispersed after a witness failed to identify him.

episodes.title: Chanute Evergreen Park mass meeting against a Black homebuilder
episodes.summary: About 300 white residents of Chanute's Evergreen park addition met at a partly built Black family's home, some carrying clubs, and agreed to demand the builder stop, otherwise they would tear the dwelling down.

episodes.title: Pursuit of an unidentified Black man after the Hagan shooting, St. Paul (1903)
episodes.summary: After a Black man grabbed Miss Mary Hagan at Eighth and Sibley streets, she fired three shots and he fled. Several men ran after him and would have used summary methods had they overtaken him. No capture reported.

episodes.title: Killing of George Johnson in Ensley
episodes.summary: Special Officer Williams of Ensley, a sanitary inspector, shot and killed George Johnson, a Black drayman, after a quarrel over a tax demand in which Johnson allegedly raised a chair. Williams gave himself up.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Joseph Erwin
episodes.summary: After Joseph Erwin, a Black man, shot and robbed Edward Lawson, a crowd of several hundred chased him through East St. Louis. Policeman Mulqueeny drew revolvers to hold back the mob, which shouted 'Lynch the negro,' brought ropes and threatened the saloon where he was held; the patrol wagon arrived in time.

episodes.title: Hunt for a Black suspect in the Seward murder, Putnam County, Indiana
episodes.summary: Searching parties scoured the Lena vicinity for a Black man thought to have murdered Mrs. Hauck Stewart, and made threats that he would be lynched if caught. Descriptions were sent across the country.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Tom Manns, Ed Morris and Charles Sanders
episodes.summary: Farmers gathered in Maysville as the three Black men accused of John Farrow's murder were tried. Shouts from mob leaders led militia to fix bayonets and hold the crowd in a square. Guardsmen prevented a lynching, and the courthouse was guarded by a cannon.

episodes.title: Assault on Frank Holland and Nelson Peters
episodes.summary: At 6:30 a.m. at the corner of Chestnut and Point streets, an act of violence occurred against two colored men who were non-union drivers employed by a firm during a teamsters' strike. The article breaks off before naming the act or attackers.

episodes.title: Lynching of Andrew Diggs
episodes.summary: A mob of 50 marched from Larkinville and took Andrew Diggs, a Black man held in the Scottsboro jail for alleged assault on a white woman, toward the woods to lynch him. Sheriff Austin resisted, was shot down, and lost his keys. Diggs's fate is not stated.

episodes.title: Lynching of William Williams
episodes.summary: A mob of several hundred lynched William Williams, a Black labor agent, on Main Street in Centerville, Miss., after he shot and killed white employee James H. Germany in a quarrel over enticing workers away. The mob chased him and shot him to death.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Wade Bennett
episodes.summary: An armed mob surrounded the Clayton jail on Monday night seeking to lynch Wade Bennett, a Black prisoner accused of killing Frank Lesuer. The jailor spirited him to a citizen's home and the mob dispersed.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Isom Strong
episodes.summary: A mob followed the sheriff who was secretly moving Isom Strong, a Black prisoner held for attempted entry into a widow's bedroom at Henderson, took him from the officers and brought him back, and prepared to lynch him. The mob dispersed after the judge's promise.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Paul Doe
episodes.summary: After a Black boy was arrested for stabbing Private William Bayne of the Twelfth cavalry, about 150 soldiers gathered at the Brackettville jail with picks and crowbars to lynch him. Major Kendall dispersed them with a guard.

episodes.title: Indianola post office affair
episodes.doubt: the threat to her life was alleged and denied; no violence occurred
episodes.summary: The article names the Indianola affair only in passing, saying President Roosevelt's comment on it gave Vardaman a boost and that the excitement over it had subsided. The text describes no acts, actors or victims.

episodes.title: Attack on the home of Andrew Cheney
episodes.summary: At midnight Saturday a posse of white men tried to batter down the door of Negro farmer Andrew Cheney to capture him. He fired through the door, wounding white farmer John Suggs, who was at the point of death; the posse left. Cheney surrendered to the sheriff.

episodes.title: Whipping of Tom Jefferson
episodes.summary: A crowd of white citizens at Graniteville, SC, gave Tom Jefferson, a Black man accused of assaulting a crippled white boy in Aiken, over fifty lashes and ordered him to leave the community at once. He had been arrested and released on a promise to leave.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Frank Clark
episodes.summary: Armed posses of Clark County farmers hunted Frank Clark, a Black man accused of cutting a white girl near Medill, Mo., intending to lynch him; other Black men were guarded or seized during the search. The mobs dispersed by July 30; Clark was arrested at Galesburg in September, convicted and legally hanged Nov. 25.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Bud Scipio
episodes.summary: After a white woman, Mrs. Maud Walker, alleged a Black man, Bud Scypo, assaulted her, a posse started in pursuit. The paper says Coffeyville is aroused and predicts he will be lynched if captured.

episodes.title: Warning notices to Black residents of Colorado, Texas (1903)
episodes.summary: A notice was placed on negro churches at Colorado, Coy, Tex., warning the colored people to leave. No date, author or further action is given.

episodes.title: Evansville race riot of 1903
episodes.summary: A race riot at Evansville, Ind., is reported only through its aftermath: a Negro named Brown, said to have caused it, was removed for safety and will be returned to Evansville. A second item names Lee Brown as precipitating the riots and sent to Jeffersonville prison; both likely refer to the same man.

episodes.title: Attack on Moses Banks
episodes.summary: A crowd of about 75 white men and boys beat Moses Banks, a Black man, with clubs, bats and stones at a Woodstock ball game and chased him to Joe Hardin's house, where he hid. The crowd hesitated at the house until the police chief and mayor arrived and jailed him. One Black man was hurt.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Joe Battle
episodes.summary: Edgecombe County officers, hearing intimations of an attempt to lynch Joseph Battle, accused of raping a white woman, moved him out of the county. Sentinels were reportedly posted to head off the deputy, who took a roundabout route to Raleigh.

episodes.title: Whipping of Bun near Fender, Georgia
episodes.summary: After a young white woman awoke to find a Black youth, Bun, at her bedside, men chased him and captured him the next morning. Several young men started with him toward Tifton jail, but he escaped. Rumor says he was severely flogged and warned to leave.

episodes.title: Texas, Maryland, dynamite explosions (1903)
episodes.summary: Unknown persons set off two dynamite explosions in Texas village, one at a stone house occupied by colored man Arch Wye and one near the Bosley lime kilns. Damage was slight. The paper says the blasts were meant to intimidate colored and foreign laborers at the quarries.

episodes.title: Hurlock election riot
episodes.doubt: election-day exchange of gunfire reported as a race war; papers say Black men fired first; the four named wounded were white; 14 Black men arrested, indicted for rioting and acquitted
episodes.summary: A crap game dispute at Hurlock led to a shootout on the night of Nov. 3; one Black man and three white men were wounded. Deputies and a posse went to the scene and fourteen Black residents were arrested.

episodes.title: Wellston church whitecapping
episodes.summary: Unknown parties destroyed Albert Boyd's tent and threw out his furniture at Wellston, then posted a notice signed by 'Citizens of Wellston' warning that a church for colored people would not be allowed and that sterner measures would follow.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Berry Henry
episodes.summary: About 25-30 armed men marched on the Polk County jail at Barlow at night seeking Black prisoner Berry Henry, held for shooting Col. and Mrs. John Beatty. Sheriff J. D. Tillis refused, the mob dispersed, and the prisoner was taken to Tampa.

episodes.title: Lynching of an unidentified man near Woodville, Mississippi (1903)
episodes.summary: After a Woodville fire on May 8, a Black man accused of setting fire to a Woodville store and of burglary confessed and was lynched by citizens of Wilkinson County about May 28. No report gives the method or the number of lynchers.

episodes.title: Killing of Joe Sanders
episodes.summary: A posse of citizens went to arrest Joe Sanders, a Black man, at Henderson, Texas, and shot him dead at his door.

episodes.title: March 1903 Bungaloo attacks in Indianapolis
episodes.summary: From about 8 to 11 p.m. a crowd of white youths, the Bungaloos, chased several Black men through downtown Indianapolis, shouting 'Kill the niggers!' Pursuers chased Bluford Williams and George Kinslow; Kinslow escaped on a street car and Williams took refuge in an office building. Police on duty did not stop it.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of John Haynes
episodes.summary: A mob of men and boys gathered at the Jackson, Tenn., county jail before dawn, intending to lynch sixteen-year-old John Haynes, accused of assaulting a white girl. They tried to break in the north door until the sheriff refused them and police dispersed the crowd.

episodes.title: Export Lumber Company strike assault, Brooklyn
episodes.summary: White handlers for the Export Lumber Company struck for higher overtime pay and threatened Black lumbermen hired to replace them. Four strikers beat one Black worker, were arrested, and were lightly fined.

episodes.title: Shooting and attempted lynching of Henry Johnson
episodes.summary: A posse shot Henry Johnson, a Black man, near Kemp; he survived. A mob at Kaufman tried to take him from jail to burn him, militia protected him, and he was tried and legally hanged at Kaufman on May 30.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Bill Grant
episodes.summary: Unknown men held up Deputy Sheriff Dean at Bainbridge, demanded jail keys and made threats as a crowd grew near the depot. The sheriff called militia to guard the jail, where the prisoner Bill Grant was held.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of William Riley and Andrew Kelly
episodes.summary: Citizens of Eatontown loaded stages and carriages with men and rushed to the Asbury Park jail to lynch three Black men accused of running over a girl cyclist. Police Chief Gravatt, warned in advance, surrounded the jail and the prisoners were moved to another lockup.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Frederick W. Williams
episodes.summary: After Williams stabbed Nelson Pixton in a Washington saloon, Pixton's white friends grabbed Williams and tried to drag him outside while the crowd shouted 'Lynch' him. The proprietor hid Williams in a back room until police arrived.

episodes.title: Lynching of Alexander Thompson
episodes.summary: A mob surrounded the jail after midnight, took negro prisoner Alex Thompson, and hanged him from a railroad trestle near Guerdon. The coroner's jury returned death at the hands of unknown persons; Black laborers then quit and the lumber plant shut down.

episodes.title: Berkley poll-tax riot
episodes.doubt: factional white political riot; those physically assaulted were white Fusionist officials; Black taxpayers driven off by armed threat
episodes.summary: Democrats of Berkley, Va., angered by county officials registering Black voters, formed a vigilance committee that drove Black residents from the streets at shotgun point into the negro quarter. Shots were fired, no one was hurt by gunfire, and County Treasurer Lyons and County Clerk Martin were badly beaten.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Jim Stevens
episodes.summary: About forty persons nearly lynched Jim Stevens, a young Black man, in Charlottesville early Saturday. He was accused of robbing a trunk in a residence and of an alleged attempted assault. He escaped and was later arrested.

episodes.title: Bath Beach manhunt for Calvin R. Ferguson
episodes.summary: After a seven-hour search, a crowd of citizens with police captured Black man Calvin R. Ferguson hiding in a swamp near Coney Island Creek. Police surrounded him and took him to the Bath Beach station as the crowd followed. The paper says the crowd's anger might have turned to punishment.

episodes.title: Killing of Melvin Fair
episodes.doubt: killed while arrested on a warrant for leaving a labor contract (peonage setting); the two white men were indicted for first-degree murder
episodes.summary: Constable James Stallings and John Lawson, with a warrant for a Black man who had left a labor contract, went to his home in Crenshaw County. They say he shot at them and they returned fire, killing Melvin Fair. Both men were arrested and charged with the killing.

episodes.title: Henrietta race riot
episodes.doubt: Herbert Dubbs's death (white) appears only in the Asheville version; Charlotte reports have whites disturbing a Black church meeting and Bird cut
episodes.summary: A white youth, Herbert Dubbs, was stabbed to death by two Black men at Henrietta, N.C., and a Black man was killed in return. A general fight followed; a white guard repulsed a Black gang, and a posse pursued the two killers.

episodes.title: Harassment of Black pedestrians by white boys in Savannah (1903)
episodes.summary: Small white boys in certain city sections interfered with colored persons; on a Sunday afternoon several ladies were mistreated. The boys were docketed and punished by their parents. The paper says the matter nearly became serious.

episodes.title: Killing of Henry Small
episodes.summary: Armed men of Chesterfield County hunted for hours for an unknown Negro who had assaulted women between Bellwood and Centralia. He was tracked to a swamp, surrounded by pickets ready to shoot on sight, and escaped by doubling back.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Brown and expulsion of Black residents from Whitesboro, Texas
episodes.summary: After Brown, a Black man, was accused of attempting to assault Mrs. Hart, a white mob hanged him at Whitesboro and he was cut down alive; over the next days whites whipped as many as seventeen Black men, fired into the Black section and drove out more than 100 residents. Mayor J. W. M. Hughes was federally indicted in 1904.

episodes.title: Lynching of Frank Robertson
episodes.summary: A party of about twenty-five men, supposed to be from Louisiana, overpowered the jailer at Bradley, took Negro prisoner Frank Robertson from jail and rode away with him. The paper reports him lynched; the body had not been found.

episodes.title: Expulsion of Black workers from the Evansville and Princeton traction line
episodes.summary: Thirty Black workers on the Evansville & Princeton traction line in Gibson County were driven from their work by white workers who said the jobs were theirs. The Black men were ordered out of the county, then returned under a contractor's agreement limiting their work, with posted warning notices.

episodes.title: Beating of Dillard Freeman
episodes.summary: After Dillard Freeman fled his employment at the Lowndes County sheriff's place, the Dixon brothers pursued him to his mother's cabin, beat him with pistols, tied a rope to him and marched him seven miles to Hayneville, then whipped him with a gin strap. The sheriff reportedly threatened him if he testified.

episodes.title: Pecaway shooting and attempted lynching
episodes.summary: In a mix-up at Pecaway, Pittsylvania county, Saturday night, Joe Echols shot a Negro, who was wounded; the Negro's friends beat Echols. Later an effort was made to lynch the Negro, but cooler heads prevailed.

episodes.title: Red Star whitecap confrontation
episodes.summary: Whitecaps who had warned Dan Johnson and Link Hudson twice to leave returned to make good their threats. The Negroes opened fire at close range and the whitecappers retreated; one or more are believed wounded.

episodes.title: Lynching of Ed McCollum
episodes.summary: A masked mob took Ed McCullom, a Black man, from the Sheridan jail early on October 7, tied him to a tree in the court house yard and shot him to death. He was said to have wounded Constable Crutchfield the week before.

episodes.title: Whipping of Henry Meredith
episodes.doubt: attackers' race not stated; a later Armstrong whipping was by Black men
episodes.summary: A posse of citizens broke open the city jail at Armstrong, Mo., took Henry Meredith, a Black boy arrested for cutting Will Boggs, and severely whipped him with harness tugs about a half mile from town, tied to a telegraph pole.

episodes.title: Needmore whitecap raid
episodes.summary: A band of fifteen to thirty Whitecappers came to the home of Black preacher John Millikin in Lewisburg, Tennessee, and shot him dead. His son-in-law John Hunter was forced on a search and fatally shot in the back; Millikin's wife was struck with a gun.

episodes.title: Clinton wash-basin incident
episodes.doubt: near-hanging only in a second-hand dispatch; the local report has an order to leave
episodes.summary: At Clinton, Mississippi, a Black man hired to cut wood washed his hands in a family bowl and sat to dinner; the ladies called for help, and the paper says a hanging was narrowly prevented, with the man escaping the house.

episodes.title: Shooting of Frank Wiley
episodes.summary: Marshal Flanagan of Metropolis, Ill., shot and seriously wounded Frank Wiley, colored, who was reportedly trying to assault the officer. The marshal was reported fully exonerated.

episodes.title: New Orleans riverfront lockout violence (September 1903)
episodes.summary: A crowd of striking longshoremen drove Negro longshoremen who were trying to work from the New Orleans wharf where the Canaries was being unloaded. Police intervened and then dispersed the strikers.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Sol Butcher
episodes.summary: A big crowd pursued Sol Butcher, a Black man who had cut Sheriff Dobbs on the head and hands while resisting arrest and fled into woods. The paper says a lynching is almost sure to result if he is captured. No killing is reported.

episodes.title: Whitecap attack on Isaiah Dillon's house
episodes.summary: White-cappers visited the home of Isaiah Dillon, an old Negro, at night and shot into the house with revolvers, with bullets passing through the bed cover where he slept. Location is the McCall's Creek neighborhood, Lincoln, Franklin and Amite counties.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Esau Lovely
episodes.summary: A mob of several hundred went to the St. Mary's parish jail to lynch Esau Lovely, a Negro prisoner accused of attacking and robbing a white woman. Senator Foster, judges and the sheriff persuaded the crowd to disperse; Lovely later pleaded guilty and was sentenced to thirty-four years.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Dick Thompson
episodes.summary: Citizens gathered in a crowd at the Centralia city jail Tuesday night about Dick Thompson, a Negro arrested for indecent exposure before school girls; violence was averted by interference. He was later fined $100 and costs.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Isaac Jones
episodes.summary: A mob of about 200 armed with clubs and carrying ropes went to the Tarrytown village jail to lynch Isaac Jones, a Black man accused of assaulting a white girl. They threatened to string him up to a telegraph pole; police said he had been moved and the crowd dispersed.

episodes.title: West Sixty-second Street riot (New York, 1903)
episodes.summary: On Sunday, July 12, Policeman Connor's arrest of two Black men on West Sixty-second Street, Manhattan, turned into a fight with Black residents; police reserves under Capt. Kear clubbed men in the crowd. A wire report two days later, disputed by the Sun, said white crowds severely beat several Black people.

episodes.title: Whitecapping threat against an interracial couple at Puncheon Run, Delaware
episodes.summary: Citizens near Dover, Del., threatened to whitecap a Black man named Smith and a white woman, Bertie Fleming, living together at Puncheon Run; officers arrested the couple on Dec. 22 as suspicious characters.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Perry Griffin
episodes.doubt: crowd of unstated race threatened a Black man accused of killing another Black man
episodes.summary: After Perry Griffin, a Black coachman, fatally shot Eli Brown outside Mount Vernon City Hall, a crowd surrounded him crying 'Lynch him' and pressed threateningly. Six policemen escorted him to the station house.

episodes.title: Vaughanville Odd Fellows hall burning
episodes.summary: Armed white men gathered at Vaughanville store after reports of a Black meeting and arms. A detachment checked the Odd Fellows hall, found it dark, and later the negro Odd Fellows hall burned; cause unknown. A proposed visit to alleged Black ringleaders was voted down.

episodes.title: Killing of Ned Roberts
episodes.summary: Members of the levee patrol shot and killed Ned Roberts, a Black levee worker, near East St. Louis on the night of June 9, during flood work; he was said to have threatened to break the dike.

episodes.title: Columbia circus lynching attempt (1903)
episodes.summary: A mob of Missouri university students at a circus in Columbia assaulted employees and demanded a negro employee be given up so they could string him up. He could not be found and escaped; the circus was allowed to proceed.

episodes.title: Bombing of Ebenezer A.M.E. Church, Evanston
episodes.doubt: attackers unknown; motives offered do not point to whites
episodes.summary: Ebenezer A.M.E. Church in Evanston, Ill., was dynamited on the night of May 15, 1903. No attacker was identified; rumor blamed policy gamblers or people offended by the pastor.

episodes.title: Union Station mob threat against Gordon Donaldson
episodes.summary: A crowd at the Union Station shouted "lynch him" and became a howling mob around Gordon Donaldson, a Black special officer who had pushed a woman with a baby. Police arrived and arrested him before any violence.

episodes.title: Intimidation of Charles Jackson at Boeuf River
episodes.summary: A posse of white citizens at Boeuf River, Louisiana, ordered Black mail carrier Charles Jackson not to return with the mail on his route and threatened him with death if he did not comply. Postal authorities were notified and dispatched an inspector.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Tom Fifer
episodes.summary: A Black farm hand, Tom Fifer, was accused of poisoning the water of Matthew Crossley's family and wounding Crossley with a rock near Brewton. The paper reports that threats of lynching were made against him.

episodes.title: Shooting of John Wells
episodes.summary: Merchant policeman Charles Highland shot John Wells, a Black porter, in the leg in the cellar of the Conservatory of Music on North Illinois Street, Indianapolis, mistaking him for a burglar while Wells was working there.

episodes.title: Killing of Richard Smith
episodes.summary: After a pay dispute, M. L. Daugherty, owner of the company, and his employee H. Ross Rogers chased and fatally cut Richard Smith, a Black worker, at Mobile; Daugherty was not indicted and Rogers was acquitted.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Vine Bryant
episodes.summary: During Vine Bryant's trial in Fulton circuit court, spectators shouting 'hang him!' surged forward to seize the Black defendant after he admitted shooting Leslie Hackett. The sheriff and deputies rushed him out and took him to Eddyville; he was sentenced to five years.

episodes.title: Hutchinson near-lynching (1903)
episodes.summary: A colored man at Hutchinson tramped on a white man's toes and there was nearly a lynching; when the colored man was jumped on, he rounded up his friends, and the white man's departure averted calling out the state troops.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Charles S. Burns
episodes.summary: A crowd followed Charles S. Burns, a Black man who had run through Thomas Jones's Fore Street restaurant with knives, shouting 'Lynch him' and 'Kill him.' He took refuge in Stone's drug store and was arrested.

episodes.title: Posse shooting of an escaped convict near Roanoke, 1903
episodes.summary: A week-earlier shooting: a posse of 12 men chased a Black convict, said to have fatally wounded a white man, and put buckshot into his face. He escaped and was later recaptured in Roanoke.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of William Hickson
episodes.summary: A posse with ropes and an angry mob of Black and white residents chased William Hickson on Whisky Chute, reportedly firing shots. Alderman Frank Holten caught him, drove him away and, with Roundsman Ryan, stood off the mob.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of James Taylor
episodes.summary: A crowd surrounded James Taylor, a Black assistant to New Rochelle's poundkeeper, after he shot a fox terrier, shouting 'Lynch him.' A policeman arrested Taylor, who was fined $3 and held for a cruelty-to-animals charge.

episodes.title: Horsewhipping of Frank Allen
episodes.summary: Frank Allen, a Negro from Gainesville, was severely horsewhipped at Demorest by C. L. Adams while Edgar Taylor held him at gunpoint, then driven out of town. The cause dated back months to a livery-stable incident with the men's niece.

episodes.title: Clubbing of Mr. Hill by Officer Palmer in Tarrytown
episodes.summary: Officer Palmer unnecessarily clubbed Mr. Hill about a week before the report, agitating the colored citizens of both villages, who secured counsel for Hill.

episodes.title: Lynching of Lamb Whitely
episodes.summary: News reported a lynching of Lamb Whitely, a Black man, on the Smithland plantation at Montgomery Landing, Concordia parish, Louisiana. A mob took him to the woods and riddled his body with bullets after he allegedly assaulted a white man.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of King Wrightman and Thompson
episodes.summary: First reports (Albany, Ga., Aug. 14) said a white man named Thompson and King Wrightman, a Black man, accused of assaulting Mrs. Mathis, were lynched together at Hartsfield, Colquitt County. Albany officials denied it the same night: officers eluded the mob and jailed both men at Moultrie.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of John Wilson
episodes.summary: Over a hundred farmers pursued John Wilson, a Black man accused of attempting to assault a white woman near Valparaiso. He escaped on a freight train, was later caught and knocked out, and farmers gathered in town muttering threats of vengeance.

episodes.title: Killing of Rafe Harvey
episodes.summary: Patrolman Harmon Miller shot Rafe Harvey, a Black man who had beaten officers Davis and Hartley and engineer Goolsby, in a stable in Liberty Lane. Officers and citizens then beat him with clubs and billies; Harvey died in jail about two weeks later.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of James Hayes
episodes.summary: Talk of lynching of a Negro held in Minneapolis on a charge of assaulting a 13-year-old girl in St. Paul; no crowd or physical action is reported.

episodes.title: Smith County, Mississippi, attacks on Black residents (1903)
episodes.summary: Near Burns, Smith County, a white party led by the Bruce brothers went after a Black man who had jumped a crop; they were ambushed and Craft, a white farmer, was mortally wounded. Whites returned fire, killed several Black people and were still hunting the man as of May 16.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of John D. Tross
episodes.summary: In New York, a negro, John D. Tross, fired four shots at picture manufacturer Otto Richter, wounding one man and causing a small riot; the headline says a crowd would lynch him. The text is cut off.

episodes.title: Pecan Grove posse shooting
episodes.summary: A constable's posse met a band of Black men, led by a white man, near Pecan Grove plantation in St. Charles parish. Three were killed and seven wounded; no posse member was hurt. Survivors fled to the swamps and were being searched for. The men were wanted for unpaid debts and had worked for the Mississippi Valley railroad.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of R. B. Williams
episodes.summary: After R. B. Williams, a colored tailor, fatally shot Clyde Langdon in his Larned shop, a mob began forming with the avowed intention of lynching him. The sheriff took the prisoner to Hutchinson; he was returned to Larned on Monday.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of George Wilson
episodes.summary: After Waite's killing, several white men who worked with him twice went to George Wilson's house seeking his life, on Saturday and the next night. Wilson escaped both times and was later arrested by police on suspicion of involvement in the killing.

episodes.title: Expulsion of Tom Clay from Muscatine
episodes.summary: Tom Clay, a Black man whose complaint led to the arrest of Bert Sheppard on a murder charge, was chased out of Muscatine the day after Sheppard was found innocent. The text does not name the pursuers.

episodes.title: Lynching of Hensley Johnson
episodes.summary: A mob from Carthage captured Hensely John, a negro said to have assaulted a four-year-old white girl, after he was released on bond, and hanged him in the public square; his body was found suspended from a telephone pole.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of John Brinkley
episodes.summary: A crowd crying 'lynch him' surged at policeman Mooney's prisoner, Brinkley, a Negro, at a factory office. Brinkley broke away, was chased several blocks and overtaken, and a teamster began lashing him. The text is cut off before the outcome.

episodes.title: Ordering out of Black railroad laborers near Sheridan, Arkansas
episodes.summary: White laborers ordered Negro laborers to leave their work on the Pine Bluff and Western railroad near Sheridan. About seventy-five Negroes camped in De Kalb township were grading; a company officer later said the trouble was over.

episodes.title: Lynching of Thomas Gilyard
episodes.summary: A mob took a Black man, accused of murdering a police officer, from the Joplin jail on April 15 and executed him. Five hundred deputies were sworn in afterward, and Black residents gathered in large numbers, with race trouble feared. The article is cut off mid-sentence after 'a mob drove'.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Law Young and William Murphey
episodes.summary: A crowd of several hundred gathered at Gladstone awaiting two Black suspects, Law Young and William Murphey, held over the shooting of William P. Harris on a train; trouble was feared. No physical attack is reported.

episodes.title: Police beating of Edward E. Wilson
episodes.summary: Police officers at the Harrison St station seized lawyer Edward E. Wilson when he refused a bailiff's order to take a seat, struck him several times, smashed his hat and held him in custody. Wilson later sued the officers for $10,000.

episodes.title: Harmony Grove assault on a Black woman (1903)
episodes.summary: Three young white men broke into a Black woman's home near Harmony Grove, Ga., threw her baby from her arms, dragged her into a field and assaulted her while neighbors were held at gunpoint. Warrants were issued.

episodes.title: Barwick whitecap raid
episodes.lists: None (not in Beck–Tolnay, Seguin–Rigby or HAL)
episodes.summary: A band of disguised whitecaps near Barwick, Ga., took Charles Lammons and his son into the woods, beat them and gave them forty-eight hours to leave the state. They chased Lee Wright, who hid in a swamp, and fired into Scott Wilson's house, fatally wounding his boy.

episodes.title: Tryon manhunt of 1903
episodes.summary: Armed mountaineers were scouring the mountains near Tryon, N.C., for a Black man said to have assaulted an 18-year-old white girl, and said a lynching would follow if he was captured.

episodes.title: Ridgetop train hold-up
episodes.summary: About twenty masked men with rifles held up L. & N. train No. 51 at a railroad construction camp near Ridgetop, searching the passengers for Will Reed, a Negro who had shot foreman Ollie Ware. Reed was not aboard; officers had arrested him earlier.

episodes.title: Lynching of William Fambro
episodes.summary: About fifteen white men fired shotguns and Winchesters into Will Fambro's home near Griffin, broke the door, fired through it and killed him, then threatened to burn the house. They withdrew after the woman was told help was coming.

episodes.title: Killing of John Swancey
episodes.summary: At a negro settlement in Waverly, Mo., a riot broke out among Black residents over two men running for alderman. Deputy Mark Crumpley shot and killed Black man John Swancey while quelling the disturbance. City Marshal Wood McGrew was beaten by the Black participants.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Willie and Otho Green
episodes.summary: Threats to lynch two jailed Black men, Willie and Otho Green, drew a mob from Clifton Forge to Covington on Saturday night. Deputy Sheriff Sizer armed a guard and militia took the prisoners away; no entry to the jail was attempted.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of John Griffin and attack on Black residents of Shawneetown
episodes.summary: A class of white men stoned Negro resorts and dives in a town after a Monday occurrence intensified feeling against Black residents. Many colored people took refuge in the country; at least fifty left within two days. No bloodshed reported.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Charles Smith
episodes.summary: A crowd of several hundred shouted 'Lynch him!' and rushed police holding Charles Smith, a Negro who robbed a lunchroom and shot two policemen. Police held the crowd back until reinforcements arrived and took him to the station-house.

episodes.title: Expulsion of Black men from Walnut, Kansas
episodes.summary: Walnut, Neosho county, refuses to allow a negro on the townsite. Four colored men have been chased away in the past thirty days.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Edward Green
episodes.summary: After a Black man was arrested by a posse for attempted assault on a young woman, Bronxville residents became furious and freely made threats of mob violence. Special guards were placed at the jail.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Jim Montgomery
episodes.doubt: also called Jim Gilmore; local papers say the crowd report was exaggerated
episodes.summary: A reported mob gathered near Chester, S.C., to lynch Jim Montgomery, a Black man who entered an aged widow's home and threatened her. Governor ordered militia to the scene, which probably prevented the lynching.

episodes.title: Death of William Rice
episodes.summary: Black hotel porter William Rice was found dead under a railroad trestle at Lawrenceville, Va. The Planet reports blood, torn hair and switches along the route, indicating several white men beat him before his death. No verdict was returned.

episodes.title: Lynching of Lee Hall
episodes.summary: A well-organized mob broke into the Wrightsville jail with a battering ram and hammers, dragged out Lee Hall, who had shot Sheriff Crawford, carried him a mile out of town, and hanged him from a tree while shooting his body.

episodes.title: Whitecapping of Fleming Brown
episodes.summary: A neighbors' 'committee of safety' went to the Brown house near Ashby at 1 a.m. and made Fleming Brown, a Black guardian, 'pay well' for beating his ward, dwarf girl Rosa Taylor. The paper says the committee has other matters to look into.

episodes.title: Portsmouth lynching threats of 1903
episodes.summary: Threats of lynching were made against two Black men, John Edwards and George Washington Griggs, accused of assaulting girls in Portsmouth. The promise of speedy trials averted violence; no crowd or action is described.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Isaac Ford
episodes.summary: Issaac Ford, a Black man accused of criminal assault on a little girl in Grayson County, Texas, hanged himself in jail. The paper reports that mob violence was threatened. No group is named.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of William Nichols
episodes.summary: A crowd of about 200 at Belle Center depot shouted 'shoot him' and 'hang him' at Black prisoner William Nichols, accused of murdering Alpha Minard. The train pulled out; at Kenton angry threats were made, but the sheriff jailed him.

episodes.title: Attempted expulsion of Black residents from Orchard Park, Oklahoma City
episodes.summary: About a dozen to forty masked, armed white men confronted a Negro occupant of a house in Orchard park, ordered him to leave within 24 hours and threatened rough usage. Officers who arrived were ordered away at gunpoint. The party returned to the spot the next night with no reported renewed attack.

episodes.title: Whitecap notice to Dennis Powell
episodes.summary: A typed notice ordering Dennis Powell, a Black man living two miles southwest of Brookhaven, to leave on pain of death, with a drawn coffin, was posted at his gate. Two men were believed responsible, and they fired two or three shots near his house.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching in South Memphis, Tennessee (1903)
episodes.summary: A Black man said to have tried to assault a woman in her Memphis home was captured in South Memphis and escaped from a mob before police arrived. The paper predicts he will probably be lynched.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Mat Kimble
episodes.summary: A posse of about forty citizens hunted for a man supposed to be a small Negro with a mustache, after the rape and murder of Emil Grundel's wife about five miles from New Braunfels. Bloodhounds were telegraphed for.

episodes.title: Lynching of Lewis Jackson
episodes.summary: Lewis Jackson, a Negro accused of assaulting a four-year-old girl, was released by the sheriff and seized near the Tampa jail by a waiting mob, emasculated, then hanged from an oak by a second mob that intercepted his carriage.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of W. S. Sanders
episodes.summary: After a Negro teamster horsewhipped Mrs. Mary E. Myers at a Bunola wharf, a crowd rushed him, dragged him down the street by his legs, and shouted "Lynch him!" Officers rescued him and jailed him.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Ben Lee
episodes.summary: Lee, a Black man accused of assaulting a girl, was reportedly warned that an attempt would be made to lynch him, so officials drove him away from Carlyle in a buggy. No mob action is described.

episodes.title: Lynching at Hattiesburg, Mississippi (October 1903)
episodes.summary: A mob lynched a Negro in Hattiesburg early on October 30, 1903, after he allegedly entered H. T. Allen's house on Monday night to assault a family member. The mob gathered about 1 o'clock and quickly accomplished its purpose.

episodes.title: Franklin County whitecapper arrests
episodes.summary: A Black man received a written warning to leave the county. Horsemen rode up to his cabin at midnight; a white posse that he had alerted surrounded and captured eight of them. Eight men were later bound over for intimidating negroes.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of John Wood
episodes.summary: Three attempts were made to lynch John Wood, a Black man charged with attacking Mrs. Julia Lind in June, at the time of the attack. The text gives no details of who acted or how. Wood was later convicted and sentenced to five years.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Fortune Ellis
episodes.summary: Fortune Ellis says J. B. Mitchell and Will Davis opened fire on his house after a dispute over picked cotton, and one bullet wounded his head. Ellis then fired on them, shooting Mitchell; he was captured in a church and held in Montgomery jail.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Samuel Johnson
episodes.summary: A mob overtook Samuel Johnson, accused of attacking a white woman near Helena, Ga., and hanged him from a limb. Johnson survived, was cut down by Black passersby and was later found dying in a hut in Macon.

episodes.title: Lower Merion manhunt for Elias Williams
episodes.doubt: pursued man may have been 'Cracker' Crummity, not Elias Williams
episodes.summary: Citizens' posse, many armed with pitchforks and clubs, resumed the hunt for Elias Williams, a Black man accused of murdering Percy White, in Lower Merion township. No violence against him is reported in this item.

episodes.title: Expulsion order against Black women in Spokane's "burnt district" (1903)
episodes.summary: Portland police ordered ten Black women out of town, after each had paid her monthly fine like white women of the district; they were then fined for vagrancy. Attorney Nuzum said the police were persecuting the colored women.

episodes.title: Whipping of Buff Wright
episodes.summary: A colored boy was whipped and driven out of Warsaw by a gang of lawless men. Hon. P. D. Hastain returned to Sedalia after a few days in Warsaw looking after the case. The date and the rest of the account are cut off in the OCR.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Charles Jefferson
episodes.summary: On the Sunday Parkhurst spoke, a crowd in Pennsylvania threatened vengeance on a Black man accused of assaulting a white child. A mob of 300 with a rope at Clayville was cowed by armed officers, and crowds at Taylorstown were fought through to the jail.

episodes.title: Threats against Rev. Charles H. Thomas
episodes.summary: In June 1903, shortly after the Wyatt lynching at Belleville, Ill., the pastor of the African Methodist church (named Rev. Charles H. Thompson in white-press digests, Rev. C. H./C. F. Thomas in Black-press reports) received letters warning him to leave town on penalty of personal injury. A Black-press report ties the repeated warnings to his outspoken condemnation of the Wyatt lynching. Senders unidentified.

episodes.title: Stoning of Preston Bland
episodes.summary: A crowd of about a thousand gathered and threw stones at Preston Bland, a Negro longshoreman, as police escorted him to the station after he was accused of shooting a man; many stones hit him and the policemen.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Stoney Ball
episodes.summary: A mob captured Stoney Ball, a Black man said to have assaulted a little Mexican girl, shot him in the hip and beat him about the head and face. Sheriff Baca intervened to save him from lynching; Ball died in the Los Lunas jail on Tuesday.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Wheeler Kimbro, Walter Stratton and Lorenzo Martin
episodes.summary: A mob assaulted three Afro-American men under arrest at Pettiford's house in Bellevue, Ohio, where Pettiford was a foreman at the shear works. The men were later charged in the murder of Otto Mischke; the paper says no crime was committed.

episodes.title: Forest parlor assault
episodes.summary: A Black man who sat in the parlor of Capt. S. B. Fairchild at Forest, Mississippi, was roughly handled by friends summoned by telephone and taken to jail; the sheriff intervened. The dispatch says a hanging was narrowly avoided.

episodes.title: Cleves town hall attack and threatened attack on Coal City
episodes.summary: A patrol was preventing an attack by indignant whites on the Negro settlement at Coal City, the dispatch says. No attack or violence by the whites is described.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching at Knightsville, Indiana
episodes.summary: After a burly Black man was said to have tried to break into Miss Mamie Goodhue's room in Knightsville, a posse quickly gathered and traced him to his home. Before reinforcements could take him, he and his family fled.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Frank Brown
episodes.summary: A mob of about 1,500 chased Frank Brown, a Negro who had shot Harry Holtzhauer, caught him and beat him severely. Police rescued him and took him to jail, where the mob tried to break in and was repelled by armed men. Friends of Holtzhauer vowed to lynch him.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Riley Park
episodes.summary: A mob of about twenty-five men came to Clarendon intending to lynch Riley Park, a Negro accused of shooting Jo Fowler. The sheriff had already removed Park, and the mob dispersed without acting.

episodes.title: Belleview Lake revolver threat (Waterbury, 1903)
episodes.summary: Per the strikers' executive committee, eight strike-breakers at Belleview lake drew revolvers on a colored man they thought had insulted them, then rode into the outskirts firing revolvers. No one was reported hurt.

episodes.title: Attacks on Black miners at Virginia City, Alabama
episodes.summary: Striking miners at Virginia City, Ala., surrounded the Negro quarters on two nights and fired a volley into the houses each night, wounding one man. They seized a Black guard, threatened him with lynching, then shot at and wounded him as he returned to camp.

episodes.title: Attack on Peter Stark by militiamen at Griffin, Georgia
episodes.summary: Soldiers from the Second Regiment ran at Peter Stark, a Black man who had drawn a knife after a dispute with a sergeant, and were about to do him serious violence. Citizens and police rescued him.

episodes.title: Attempted lynchings of Joe Scott and expulsion of Black residents from Montevideo, Minnesota
episodes.summary: After a young lady was murdered, a mob gathered at Montevideo, Minnesota to lynch the Black suspect, who was kept out of their way. The mob then turned on Mormon missionaries and threatened them; that threat is not coded here.

episodes.title: Thomasville posse shooting of Bill Davis
episodes.summary: A marshal and five men went to arrest Bill Davis, a Black man. Davis fired on them with a shotgun and escaped through a window. The posse fired back and pursued him. McMillan and Guess were lightly wounded, and whites chastised some Black onlookers.

episodes.title: 1903 Bronx race riot
episodes.summary: After a Negro allegedly stabbed white man John Finnessy in the Bronx, a crowd of about 150 white men hunted and beat Negroes through the night, driving them into homes. Four Negroes were beaten in Kanze's saloon until police intervened.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of French near Fort Logan
episodes.summary: Near Fort Logan, soldiers rescued a white woman from a man named French, who was said to have assaulted her, and would have lynched him had the sheriff not arrived. The article gives 'last Friday night' as the date.

episodes.title: Mutilation of George Houston
episodes.summary: A mob of about 100 masked, armed men surrounded a carriage carrying Black hackman George Houston in Tampa, seized him from City Detective Bell, bound and mutilated him at the gun club grounds, and left him there. Police found him and took him to a hospital.

episodes.title: Killing of Steve Williams
episodes.summary: Bailiff Alfred Moree shot and killed Black man Steve Williams in a field at Isabella, Ga., over costs owed. The paper calls the killing justifiable; no arrest had been made.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching at Marion, Ohio (1903)
episodes.doubt: single editorial reference; date uncertain
episodes.summary: A mob at Marion, Ohio, on a Sabbath evening tried to lynch a Black man, according to an Atlanta Constitution report the editorial cites. The text gives no result, custody or specific acts.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Ore Brown
episodes.summary: Railroad men threatened to lynch Ore Brown, a Black man accused of attempting to assault two girls near the Capitol in Madison. Police captured him, took him to the city prison and guarded him, preventing any crowd from gathering.

episodes.title: 1903 Morgan Park lynching attempt and expulsion order
episodes.summary: After a Halloween prank led police chief to strike a Negro girl, her brother killed the chief. A mob formed to lynch the Negro, but officers got him to jail. Suburb of Chicago; exact place not named.

episodes.title: Averted lynching of Frank Brown
episodes.summary: Frank Brown, a Black man alleged to have killed Charles Scott, was taken to Muskogee. A lynching was narrowly averted; a mob at Checotah and shots were exchanged. The text does not say who the mob was or what it did against Brown.

episodes.title: Threat against a Black rural mail carrier in Lincoln County, Mississippi
episodes.summary: In Lincoln County, Mississippi, the people told the Inspector that a Negro would not be permitted to perform star-route mail service, and threatened him with tar and feathers if he sided with the Negro as at Indianola.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Bert Hazelock
episodes.summary: A crowd of white men chased Bert Hazelock, a Black man, after a street brawl in Albany, shouting 'Lynch the nigger.' A thrown stone shattered his arm, and the crowd surrounded the house he entered until an officer with a revolver held them off and took him to the station.

episodes.title: Attack on Deb Flynn in Marinette
episodes.summary: A crowd of visitors at a street carnival in Mariette, Wis., started after Black man Deb Flynn with hammers and nearly killed him, resenting his walk with a white girl. Company I of the Second Regiment rescued him; he was hidden overnight and spirited out of town.

episodes.title: Lynching of Bob Bryant and Will Morris
episodes.summary: Two Black men, Bob Bryant and Will Morris, accused of murdering W. H. Legg, were taken from officers by 200 armed farmers and hanged to the Yazoo bridge at Haynes' Bluff, Mississippi, before daylight Sunday. Bryant had confessed, implicating Morris.

episodes.title: Lynching of Benjamin Gorman
episodes.summary: Benjamin Gorman, colored, was captured and lynched near Americus on the evening of May 29 for the alleged murder of farmer Shelley Kent, killed in a field near Church Hill, Webster County, on May 28.

episodes.title: Bristol State Street disturbance (1903)
episodes.summary: After a Black man pushed a white woman off the sidewalk and a white man struck him, a crowd gathered on State Street in Bristol shouting "shoot" and "lynch." The Black men were quickly hustled away; no one was harmed.

episodes.title: Lynching of John Osborne
episodes.summary: A lynching party of several hundred people took John Osborne, a Black man accused of assaulting a white woman, from two officers conveying him to the Union county jail and lynched him about two miles from Indian Trail. Guard Frank Kezziah fired a shot before being disarmed.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Adam Hunt
episodes.summary: About fifty men went to Sheriff Thompson's home after midnight at Roxboro and demanded the jail keys to lynch Adam Hunt, a Negro accused of killing Wilkins. The sheriff said he did not have access to the jail and the crowd was convinced.

episodes.title: Memphis manhunt for George Morgan
episodes.summary: After a Black man, George Morgan, shot and killed German brewery worker Adolph Heinz in Memphis, German residents formed posses searching for him with the avowed purpose of lynching him. Morgan had not been captured by late hour.

episodes.title: Atlanta messenger boys' attacks on Black telegraph messengers
episodes.summary: After Western Union and Postal Telegraph fired 200 white messenger boys and hired Black men, boys banded together as a mob. Six boys jumped and badly bruised one Black messenger at Western Union before office staff rescued him; the mob kept attacking messengers leaving the office.

episodes.title: Killing of Jim Nichols
episodes.summary: Constable Hugo Schultz went to arrest Will Nichols, wanted for shooting a railroad conductor, at his home near Forest, Kentucky. Jim Nichols, who tried to prevent the arrest, was shot during a struggle over the constable's revolver and died twelve days later.

episodes.title: Fayette whippings (1903)
episodes.summary: Men disguised as white caps dragged a Black man and two Black women from their homes at night and publicly whipped them. The man was beaten badly enough to need physicians; the women were taken to the town outskirts and ordered to leave and not return. Many Black residents are leaving Fayette.

episodes.title: Evansville mob assault on John Hawkins
episodes.summary: A mob chased and assaulted John Hawkins, a Black man, on Evansville streets on the evening of July 28, 1903. Jacob Keil was fined and jailed; Albert Merkel and George Walters were arrested.

episodes.title: Pursuit and capture of Calvin Baker
episodes.summary: A posse was out scouring the woods for Calvin Baker, a fifteen-year-old Negro boy accused of attempting an assault on a five-year-old girl in Phenix City. The paper says he will likely be lynched if caught.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of James Beran
episodes.doubt: race only in one paper's deck
episodes.summary: Male citizens of North Royalton hunted the man accused of assaulting a school teacher and found him Monday evening. A threatening crowd gathered where he was held, and officers moved him secretly to the Cleveland county jail.

episodes.title: Killing of Eugene Burke
episodes.lists: None (not in Beck–Tolnay, Seguin–Rigby or HAL)
episodes.summary: A mob of about 200, begun by packing-house employees and idlers, pursued Eugene Burk, a Black hotel worker, down railroad tracks. A young man with a revolver overtook him and shot him dead. The shooter, said to be Anderson, had not been arrested.

episodes.title: Leesburg lynching tree incident
episodes.summary: After Black guardsmen felled a tree at Leesburg, Second Cavalry men pursued them and fired ball cartridges, and sergeants captured four. Townspeople talked of lynching; the sheriff and mayor demanded the prisoners, and one guardsman was fined.

episodes.title: Macon Western Union messenger strike
episodes.summary: White Western Union messenger boys at Macon struck in early January 1903, and when Black messengers replaced them threatened to mob them; citizens petitioned for their discharge.

episodes.title: Perry Hill church shooting
episodes.summary: Three or four white men from Columbia, including Tom McDonald, fired several shots at a crowd of Black churchgoers at Perry Hill church after a dispute over a drink; Lewis Thompson was struck in the hand. Black pursuers pelted their hack with rocks and briefly held it.

episodes.title: Whipping of Dave Stokes
episodes.summary: Marshal T. H. Blizzard and Theo Rogers whipped Negro Dave Stokes at Soperton a few nights before Jan. 6. Stokes's friends then fired on Marshal Blizzard; no one was hit.

episodes.title: Notices ordering Black residents out of the Egypt community, Kaufman County, Texas
episodes.summary: Notices were posted in the Egypt community near Terrell, warning all Negroes to leave at once under penalty of their lives, signed "Mobbers." The posting followed a criminal assault on Mrs. Whitworth the previous week.

episodes.title: Lynching of Jim Nelson
episodes.summary: Armed men stopped a buggy carrying Jim Nelson, held for an alleged attempted outrage, about three miles from Jefferson, Chesterfield County, took him and hanged him. The body hung all Sunday and was buried near the road after a coroner's inquest.

episodes.title: Braggs race riot of May 1903
episodes.summary: A race riot broke out at Braggs, eighteen miles northeast of Muskogee, Indian Territory, and a Negro was reported ambushed. Telephone service was cut and six deputies went to the scene. The text is truncated and gives no casualties or attackers.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Isaac Adkins
episodes.summary: A posse under Deputy-Sheriff Halight pursued and captured Isaac Adkins, a Black man accused of attacking a white girl in Fishkill. A crowd threatened vengeance and a committee chose a hanging site and bought a rope, but Adkins was taken secretly to Poughkeepsie jail.

episodes.title: West End mob letter to M. E. McKelley
episodes.summary: An anonymous letter dated August 23 signed 'West End mob' ordered M. E. McKelley, the only Black family on Wichita's West Side, to move within ten days. Police were shown the letter and detectives sought the writer.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of D. R. Stokes
episodes.summary: A large body of white men seized Rev. Dr. Stokes, a Black preacher campaigning against prohibition, during his speech in Gregg county, took him to the Sabine river and prepared to hang him. A white man who had demanded the lynching then spared him on condition he never return, and he was driven out of the county.

episodes.title: Killing of T. J. Thomas
episodes.summary: Mounted Policeman Jesse F. Greek shot and killed T. J. Thomas, a Black man, at Jacksonville on Wednesday night after going to stop a quarrel; Thomas allegedly advanced on him with an open razor. Greek's hand was cut.

episodes.title: Boaz hanging ordeal and expulsion
episodes.doubt: non-fatal hanging to force a confession, then expulsion; dossier reads it as mob assault
episodes.summary: Near Boaz, a dozen men strung two Black men up in the woods by nooses over trees until nearly dead, then cut them down. After they confessed to a meat theft, they were driven out of town. Townspeople announced they would not tolerate Black citizens.

episodes.title: Milltown, Georgia, committee beating of 1903
episodes.summary: After a fight in which Black engineer Seab Sharp beat white conductor Charlie Clanton at Naylor, Clanton's friends started out to find Sharp at Milltown; he dodged them and got away.

episodes.title: Whitecapping of George and Amelia Guenther
episodes.doubt: Amelia Guenther Black, George Guenther white
episodes.summary: Twelve masked men with shotguns and revolvers surrounded the Guenther home five miles from Sandusky and fired into the bed where George Guenther, white, and his colored wife lay, injuring both slightly and riddling the furniture. This was the third attack since their marriage two weeks earlier.

episodes.title: Air-rifle shooting of a Black woman in Savannah (1903)
episodes.summary: Some white boys in a Savannah neighborhood seriously shot a colored woman with an air rifle the Sunday before a white boy was killed by a trolley. No attempt was made to apprehend the shooter.

episodes.title: Thebes lynching and attack on Black construction camps
episodes.summary: A mob of angry farmers lynched an unknown Negro youth of about 17 near Santa Fee, Illinois, Sunday afternoon, for allegedly attempting to assault a farmer's 10-year-old daughter. The mob then attacked a colony of Negro bridge workers living in tents, burning the tents and shooting many.

episodes.title: Killing of Albert Dennis
episodes.summary: Special policeman Milan E. McNamara shot and mortally wounded a Black man, supposed to be Albert Dennis, on the sidewalk outside the Great Northern theater in Chicago after ejecting him. Dennis died at the county hospital.

episodes.title: Lynching of Allen Small
episodes.summary: A mob came to the Moore county jail at Lynchburg, Tenn., demanded prisoner Allen Small, a Black man charged with attempted assault, and after breaking through the jail doors shot him in his cell. Sheriff Stevenson and police fought the mob.

episodes.title: Lynching of Dennis Head
episodes.summary: A mob near Chinquepin, Aiken County, S.C., killed Dennis Head and Jessie Butler on Thursday night after postmaster William Hall was murdered. The men were said to know the whereabouts of suspect Edwards, and the mob was reported still hunting Edwards and possibly Lonny Johnson.

episodes.title: Whipping of Annie Miller
episodes.doubt: whipping ordered by a committee of white and Black residents; the lynching of the jailed men was planned, not attempted
episodes.summary: A committee of white and black residents of Bossier tried Monie Miller, who confessed to writing threatening letters, and sentenced her to a public whipping. A special committee of three lashed her near Vanceville before hundreds of people, nearly unconscious, and she was to be expelled from the parish.

episodes.title: Hoisington warning notices (1903)
episodes.summary: Several typewritten notices were posted around Hoisington one night the week before, warning Negroes to leave town. Rumor said enforcement would be tried Monday night, but no disturbance occurred.

episodes.title: Lynching of Reuben Elrod
episodes.summary: About 50 white men came to a house near Piedmont at about 10 p.m., shot and killed Reuben Elrod, a Black man, whipped three Black women there and warned them to leave the country. The inquest verdict was death at the hands of parties unknown.

episodes.title: Whitecapping of John Lee
episodes.summary: John Lee, a colored teamster who said he threw flour on Doc Bacon, was reported white-capped on Saturday night and has not been seen since; the paper presumes he left the county.

episodes.title: Killing of Mooney Allen
episodes.doubt: crowd joined by the sheriff chased and killed him; line between posse killing and lynching unclear
episodes.summary: A pursuing mob of hundreds chased Mooney Allen, colored, through the streets of Beaumont after Sheriff Landry's posse captured him and he broke from a carriage. More than a hundred shots were fired and he was killed.

episodes.title: Lorain mob attack on Charles Hall and Robert Pleasant
episodes.summary: About 400 whites in Lawrence pursued two Black men, Charles Hall and Charles Pleasant, after a razor altercation with a white man. The men took refuge in a barroom, whose front the mob battered with stones; police restored order, and the mob fired some shots.

episodes.title: Lynching of William (Bee) Washington
episodes.lists: None (not in Beck–Tolnay, Seguin–Rigby or HAL)
episodes.summary: William Washington, a Black man said to have killed white man Stanley Woods near Talbert on the Louisiana-Mississippi line, was lynched on Saturday night a short distance into Mississippi, according to a New Orleans report.

episodes.title: Oakwood handcar ambush
episodes.summary: A posse of about twelve citizens at Oakwood placed a plank on the track and fired on three negro burglars who were fleeing on a hand car, running a fight through the village. One posse member was slightly wounded; the burglars escaped.

episodes.title: Killing of the Laurant family near Florenville, Louisiana
episodes.summary: A race riot at the Parker settlement on Tallyscheek creek, St. Tammany parish, left four Negroes of the Larton family killed and two wounded after white citizens acted against them following a dispute at a store. Deputies made arrests.

episodes.title: Mob attack on Leslie Triplett
episodes.summary: A mob of white hoodlums attacked Leslie Triplett, an Afro Irish policeman, at West Point, Miss., on the 12th inst. He was still suffering from his injuries when the notes were written.

episodes.title: Killing and cremation of Albert Washington
episodes.summary: Two Shreveport police officers overtook and shot Edward Porter, a Black man said to have fled with bloody clothes after the murder of Mrs. Matthews. He was not in custody and was shot down as he tried to escape. The body was afterwards burned by persons seeking revenge.

episodes.title: Killing of L. A. Planving
episodes.summary: Prof. L. A. Planving, Black educator and friend of Booker T. Washington, was shot from ambush and killed near Oscar, La., on the Sunday before this issue. The paper rejects the white account that he gave incendiary speeches and calls the killing a murder by white men.

episodes.title: Reported lynching of Charles Young
episodes.doubt: all lynching reports are hearsay relayed from Ragland; the Birmingham Age-Herald denied it
episodes.summary: A report from Ragland reached Birmingham that Charles Young, a Negro who worked at a Seaboard Air Line railroad camp, was lynched near Coal City, St. Clair County, for allegedly attempting to assault a white woman at her home.

episodes.title: Armourdale mob chase and drowning
episodes.doubt: pursued man drowned himself; the crowd did not reach him
episodes.summary: A man who called at a widow's home, demanded money and held her for over three hours was accused of assault. A crowd formed to chase him, and before they reached him he jumped into a river and drowned himself rather than be lynched.

episodes.title: Expulsion of Abner Debleu from Chinook
episodes.summary: Citizens of Chinook told Black man Abner Debleu to leave town over laziness. When he refused, a lynching or tar and feathers was threatened. Townsmen raised $2.75 and he was shipped to Astoria by steamer.

episodes.title: Averted lynching at Victoria, Mississippi
episodes.summary: About 500 people assembled at Victoria when two Black men suspected of murdering Oneal Jones were brought there for a preliminary hearing. A lynching was expected but did not occur; the men were returned to jail in Holly Springs.

episodes.title: Attack on the "Our Kids" troupe at Home City, Kansas
episodes.summary: After being run out of Home City, the Black vaudeville performers went to Marysville, where citizens would not let them stop even long enough to eat. The paper gives no force beyond the refusal.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of John Thompson
episodes.summary: A crowd of nearly 300 surrounded a trolley car in Philadelphia to seize John Thompson, a Black man said to have assaulted a white man. Firemen from truck No. 11 fought through the mob and rescued him; police arrived later and dispersed the crowd.

episodes.title: Lynching of Crane Green
episodes.summary: A lynching bee was held near Warren, Ark., on Sunday night, July 19, against Crane Green, a Negro accused of assaulting a white girl. He had been arrested at Lanark and was being taken to jail; the article is cut off before the lynching is described.

episodes.title: Whipping of a Black woman at Blue Ridge Springs, Virginia
episodes.summary: A party of white men whipped a Black woman near Blue Ridge Springs, Virginia, on a Saturday night late in July 1903; both races then armed, buying guns at Roanoke.

episodes.title: Newmarket hotel whipping
episodes.summary: Two young Black men who ordered a meal at the New Market hotel were insolent when told to leave. A relative knocked them down and kicked them out, and a crowd of white men gave each fifty lashes with a rawhide whip.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of James Little
episodes.summary: A mob of farmers, striking molders and boat hands gathered at New Baltimore as the accused Black prisoner James Little was brought back for arraignment. Deputy Sheriff Gould disarmed the girl's father, Joseph Cole, who had drawn a revolver, and the prisoner reached the jail safely.

episodes.title: Reported expulsion of Black residents from Eldorado, Illinois
episodes.doubt: known only from one sentence in Senator Tillman's remarks; date unknown
episodes.summary: Senator Tillman's remarks, as printed, say the people of Eldorado, Ill., recently chased every Negro out of the town. No group or method is named beyond that.

episodes.title: Lynching of Frank Brown
episodes.summary: After Jim Brown allegedly shot overseer Connell and fired at owner McDade on the Knox Point plantation, a posse of white men pursued him, captured him, disarmed him and hanged him to a tree near McDade station, Bossier.

episodes.title: Monessen saloon riot
episodes.summary: During a late-night riot in a Monessen saloon between white and colored coal miners, George Williams, colored, fatally shot Lemuel Gilmore, white. Williams and William Griffey escaped; a crowd of white miners pursued them, avowing intent to lynch Williams if caught.

episodes.title: Pursuit of a Black strikebreaker on the Alton railroad, Chicago (1903)
episodes.summary: Unionists organized a hunt for a Black strikebreaker working at the Alton railroad freight in Chicago; he feared they meant to lynch him and jumped into the river. Police prevented his death.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Thomas Vaughn
episodes.summary: After Thomas Vaughn, a Black man of Philadelphia, attempted to murder his wife on Swedesboro's main street, there were threats to lynch him on the spot. He was taken safely to jail.

episodes.title: Libby whitecap attacks
episodes.summary: A Kuklux band reportedly whipped Jess Robertson's horse to death, fired into the home of Black schoolteacher Jim Morris, drove his family out and carried him away; Morris is missing and feared murdered. Clothes were found in the woods.

episodes.title: Killing of Mose Hart
episodes.summary: Mose Hart, a Black man on trial before Mayor Young for carrying a concealed weapon, shot his wife and fired at officers, then fled. A large armed crowd surrounded him in a house, which was set on fire; he ran out and was riddled with bullets.

episodes.title: Attempted expulsion of Black residents from Ballinger, Texas
episodes.summary: Notices posted in Ballinger threatened to do bodily harm to negroes if they did not at once leave town. Mayor John Hoffer proclaimed they would not be molested and appointed citizens as deputy marshals to stop any molestation.

episodes.title: Expulsion of Black residents from Fremont, Ohio
episodes.summary: On the night of May 11, 1903, Clauss shear works strikers stormed the house of a Black family in Fremont, Ohio, and about two dozen Black residents and their families fled to Oberlin.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Arthur Robinson
episodes.summary: An angry mob of several hundred pursued Arthur Robinson, a colored depot porter, with threats of lynching. A squad of policemen arrived at the barn where he was at bay and saved him. Robinson had struck John Hillis with an iron bar; Hillis may die.

episodes.title: Whitecapping of William Noblett
episodes.summary: Several weeks before November 1903, a whitecap band raided near Farmington, Marshall County, and badly beat Black couple William Noblett and his wife. Seven suspects were arrested, released after a preliminary hearing, and indicted by the grand jury on November 18.

episodes.title: Pfeiffer Quarry spur camp shooting
episodes.summary: Shots were fired into a camp of Negro laborers at the Pfeiffer quarries, seven miles north of Batesville, and the frightened workers left camp and fled to Batesville a day or two before the report. No one is reported hurt.

episodes.title: Martin's Ferry mob of May 1903
episodes.summary: After an alleged assault on a white woman, several hundred citizens gathered at the Martin's Ferry building holding a Black suspect taken in Wheeling. No attempt was made to seize him; officers quieted the crowd, which dispersed in about an hour.

episodes.title: Mob attack on a robbery victim at the American Tract Society Building
episodes.summary: A white mob near the American Tract Society Building in New York shouted "Kill the nigger" and beat a Black man after he knocked down a robber; a club broke up the mob and he left under police protection.

episodes.title: Dynamiting of Jasper Smitherman's house
episodes.summary: A number of white men dynamited the house of Jasper Smitherman, a Black man said to have paid attentions to a white woman, expecting him to be home. Smitherman was not found and left town with the woman; white men said they would watch for him.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Hugh Armstead
