episodes.summary: After Hugh Armstead, a Negro, shot Patrick Butler, a crowd of at least 500 men chased him to the Monongahela River, crying "Lynch him." Police fought the crowd to protect him and took him to jail.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of John Jackson
episodes.summary: John Jackson, a Black man accused of assaulting Mrs. Harry Mason at Zwolle, La., was captured, identified and nearly lynched near Many; an attempt to lynch him at Zwolle failed when a constable took him to the parish prison.

episodes.title: Shooting of Jesse Bagents
episodes.summary: On Saturday night, December 26, 1903, three white men on the Monticello road near the four-mile post from Brookhaven, Lincoln County, fired a shotgun at Jesse Bagents and his younger brother after the two passed and greeted them. Jesse was shot in the back and left for dead; his brother escaped and reported him killed. Coroner Lambright, riding out the next morning to hold an inquest, found him alive in a cabin, 'likely to recover' (Brookhaven Leader, Dec. 30). A syndicated column in January 1904 called it 'another whitecap murder'; no report confirms a death. It came during the Lincoln County whitecap campaign that killed Henry List (Nov.) and Eli Hilson (Dec. 19-20).

episodes.title: Expulsion of John Johnson from Decatur, Indiana
episodes.summary: A race riot against Black residents occurred in Decatur, Indiana, on Friday night, July 3. Will Foreman, leader of the mob, was fined $1 for assault and battery, and no other arrests were made. The text gives no acts of violence.

episodes.title: Lenox Hotel shooting
episodes.summary: Policemen who spent the night in a Black and Tan saloon teased waiter Jefferson Sanders, seized him and beat him on the head with pistol butts. Sanders then shot and killed Policeman Peters and wounded Sergeant Gilhooley and Policeman Russo, and was clubbed after his pistol emptied.

episodes.title: Lynching of Huse Thompson
episodes.lists: None (not in Beck–Tolnay, Seguin–Rigby or HAL)
episodes.summary: Huse Thompson, a Black man arrested after a knife attack on City Marshal Keegan at Robeline, was taken and hanged by unknown parties on the night of January 3 or before dawn January 4. A coroner's jury returned a verdict of death at unknown hands.

episodes.title: Killing of Eli Hilson
episodes.summary: Eli Hilson, a Black man living eight miles from Brookhaven, was killed while driving home alone in his buggy, after a earlier whitecap warning to leave that he disregarded. The paper says a second Black man was murdered by whitecaps in the same part of Lincoln County within a month.

episodes.title: White Hall sawmill whitecapping
episodes.summary: Eleven white men, charged with whitecapping, went in a body to a sawmill operated by Black workers near White Hall, Arkansas, and ordered the Black workers out under threat of violence, shutting the mill down. The men were arrested and taken to Helena.

episodes.title: Killing of Jennie McCall
episodes.summary: A mob surrounded the house of Jennie McCall, a Black woman, near Jennings, Florida, while seeking her husband, and fired a volley into the house, killing her. A posse was reported in pursuit of the assailants.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of John Coppedge
episodes.summary: John Coppedge, a Black man convicted of burglary, was hurried to the North Carolina penitentiary from Nash county because of strong threats of lynching. The threatening group is not described and no physical move is reported.

episodes.title: Snyder hotel crowd of 1903
episodes.summary: A crowd gathered and went to a hotel demanding a Black packer brought by a traveling man; he was not found. Residents were determined to permit no Black person to remain in Snyder.

episodes.title: Lynching of George Kennedy
episodes.summary: A mob of about 100 men lynched George Kennedy, a Black man, at Taylorown near Shreveport on Sunday night. He was said to have assaulted a railroad conductor and been found armed in wait to kill him. The mob dispersed quietly.

episodes.title: Killing of Dan Washington
episodes.summary: Constable DeBerry shot and killed Dan Washington, a Black man, in the courthouse at Fairfield, Texas, after a claimed threat. The negro reportedly did not fire; the constable shot five times.

episodes.title: Killing of Charles Potter
episodes.doubt: a former employer killed him, claiming self-defense; the farmers' pursuit had ended; Black residents protested
episodes.summary: Residents hunted Potter, a Black farm hand discharged by farmer Isaac Chase, after he allegedly tried to kill Chase and fled. When he reappeared at the farm, Chase shot him dead with a shotgun. Chase was arrested by the sheriff.

episodes.title: Posse pursuit of Gus Epps
episodes.summary: A posse of about twenty armed young men took a train after Epps, a Black man who had cut Vinson, and chased him near Twelve Pole creek, firing an estimated fifty shots. He escaped across the creek, and the hunt continued into Ohio until he was arrested in Ironton.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of W. P. Richardson
episodes.summary: After a Black butcher, W. P. Richardson, grabbed a white woman at a Tampa street car crossing and resisted arrest, several gentlemen rushed up intending summary vengeance and vowed to cut his throat. The deputy calmed the crowd; no attack is reported.

episodes.title: Suspected lynching of Cleveland Kelly
episodes.doubt: killing believed by the correspondent and one digest; no body or inquest found
episodes.summary: A posse with a hunted Black man, Cleveland Kelly, on his trail near a swamp in Newton County, Georgia. The men returned saying they lost him and gave up. Kelly disappeared, and the paper believes he was lynched, though no killing is reported.

episodes.title: Lynching of Joe Drake
episodes.summary: A mob of about 100 men overpowered Jailer Andrew Crockett, took Joe Drake from the Lauderdale County jail, dragged him to a spot about 150 yards away, hanged him and fired about fifty shots into his body.

episodes.title: Whipping of Jim Pruitt
episodes.summary: White cappers took Jim Pruitt, a colored man, from his house on a Tuesday night in the Cross Anchor section and gave him a severe whipping. They threatened him and his wife with death if they spoke of it.

episodes.title: Cambridge Uncle Tom's Cabin disturbance
episodes.doubt: beatings rest on one clause in a hostile editorial
episodes.summary: After a traveling Uncle Tom's Cabin company presented its play at Cambridge, Md., a number of Black residents were beaten. The article does not say who the attackers were.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Walter Simmons
episodes.summary: Passengers of a derailed Creve Coeur streetcar attempted to lynch Walter Simmons, a Black man found hiding near the wreck. Superintendent Meier removed him from the crowd and took him to Delmar, where an officer took custody.

episodes.title: Pursuit of a Black man in Chester County, Pennsylvania (1903)
episodes.doubt: single editorial sentence
episodes.summary: At the same time as the Delaware lynching, a crowd of whites in Chester county, Pennsylvania, was after a Negro said to have shot and killed a farmer. The text does not say what the crowd did.

episodes.title: Whitecap shooting on the Day place, Amite County, Mississippi
episodes.summary: Unknown whitecaps fired several shots into the houses of two Negro families on the Day place in Amite county last week; an old Negro was seriously wounded in the melee. The paper attributes it to a fresh agitation of the Negro question.

episodes.title: Cross County whitecapping and killing of John H. Brown
episodes.doubt: the one killed was a white detective, ambushed during a whitecap campaign against Black tenants; B-T lists it as a lynching
episodes.summary: Whitecaps posted notices ordering all Negroes off R. M. Fallis' plantation in southern Cross County. On the last allowed night, buckshot was fired through a window, killing detective R. C. Brown, who had been sent to stop the exodus.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Harry Irvin
episodes.summary: A mob of fifty or sixty armed men, led by brothers of an 11-year-old girl allegedly assaulted, chased Harry Irvin, a Black man, into a house at Monteith, Effingham County, and prepared to force entry. A constable arrived, persuaded them, and took him to Savannah.

episodes.title: Killing of Thomas Williams
episodes.doubt: night killing by unknown parties; the wife accused one white man
episodes.summary: Thomas Williams, a Black farmer near Ocklocknee, was called from his house at night by unknown parties and shot dead on Friday. A white man was accused by his wife but has an alibi; whites warned families and prepared for a threatened race war.

episodes.title: Lynching of Amos Jones
episodes.summary: A mob of about 500 seized Amos Jones, a Black prisoner who had shot jailer Sexton, cut him from his cell with chisels, dragged him through town and hanged and shot him at Gordon creek bridge. Sheriff Batson was tied up and the fire brigade refused to disperse the mob.

episodes.title: Anonymous letters to Black tenants near Clarendon, Arkansas
episodes.summary: Anonymous letters told negroes of the Fowler-Coburn neighborhood near Clarendon that leaving the country was best, and a general exodus seemed imminent. Landlords went out and promised protection, and the negroes agreed to stay.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching at Clarendon, Arkansas (1903)
episodes.summary: A mob gathered in Clarendon on the night before, seeking to lynch a Negro on trial there, and the sheriff was kept busy protecting his prisoner. It was thought the mob would return that night.

episodes.title: Manhunt for Harry Thomas (1903)
episodes.summary: Searching parties of white men hunting Harry Thomas, accused with Shack Johnson of assaulting a watchman, broke into Mollie Smith's house in Winchester on Aug. 31, 1903, firing revolvers; a lynching was said to be certain had he been found.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of George and Charles Pittman
episodes.summary: A lynching party was being formed in Lawrence County to punish George and Charlie Pittman, Black men said to be unruly at religious services. Sheriff Garrett, with two deputies, took them to Jackson; the sheriff was wounded during the arrest.

episodes.title: Resignation of mail clerk I. Bowman at Mansura, Louisiana
episodes.doubt: rests on Bowman's word; the officer denied any mob
episodes.summary: A mob at Mansura, La. threatened L. Bowman, a Black mail clerk, and he resigned because of the threats. No violence is reported.

episodes.title: Hartford City lynch mob
episodes.summary: A crowd of about 500 gathered at the Hartford City jail demanding the keys to search for two Black men said to have mutilated a 19-year-old white boy. The sheriff let them search, they found no one, and they dispersed. A posse of about 300 had earlier hunted the men.

episodes.title: Warning notice to Black residents of Waxahachie, Texas
episodes.doubt: one notice the paper treated as a prank
episodes.summary: A typed warning notice reading 'ALL NEGROS ARE WARNED TO LEAVE THIS TOWN IN 4 DAYS' was found posted on a telephone pole near the Central Passenger station. The paper thinks a boy may have written it; Negroes who read it did not seem alarmed.

episodes.title: Albany Elk pin incident
episodes.summary: A mob of about ten white men in Albany, Ga., confronted a Black man wearing an Elk pin, said Black people could not wear the emblem in the town, and, with knives drawn, forced him to take the pin off himself.

episodes.title: Dynamiting of Fannie Robinson's house
episodes.summary: At about 2 a.m. on March 20, dynamite was placed on the front door step of the house of colored woman Fannie Robinson in Christiansburg, partly demolishing it; she and her children escaped unhurt. No clue to the perpetrators was found; damage estimated at $500.

episodes.title: Henderson circus shooting
episodes.doubt: white accounts say Bruce returned armed and fired first, killing Officer Robertson
episodes.summary: At a show in Henderson, police forcibly removed a Black man who had taken a reserved seat. After the show he walked up to policemen Robertson and Crockett and began shooting; they returned fire and killed him. Robertson was seriously wounded and Crockett slightly.

episodes.title: Red Oak cotton pickers' cabin shooting
episodes.doubt: Texas dispatch: both men wounded; Houston wire: both killed
episodes.summary: An unknown party fired a volley of shots into a Black cabin on J. T. Sullivan's farm near Red Oak, wounding George Hill in the shoulder and Jess Bruce in the arm, while they were picking cotton.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Maynard Hudson
episodes.summary: Early on Aug. 8 a mob of over one hundred white men tried to secure and hang Maynard Hudson, a Black man accused of attempting to assault a white girl. They stormed the Hillsboro jail and bruised a policeman, but the prisoner had been taken away by the sheriff. The mob dispersed, though it threatened to renew the attempt.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Daniel Reed
episodes.summary: An angry mob gathered in Alexandria, Indiana after a Black saloon porter, Daniel Reed, cut Martin Taylor and attacked Mrs. Richard Hollis. The mob pursued him with intent to lynch; he was chased a mile into the country and lost in darkness.

episodes.title: Killing of Andrew Render
episodes.summary: Hartford town Marshal Enon Paris shot and killed Andy Render, a Black man, during a disturbance on the street-fair weekend, after Render allegedly advanced on him. Paris surrendered to the sheriff and his case was expected before the grand jury.

episodes.title: Beach's Still dance shooting
episodes.summary: Two white men reportedly locked the doors of a building where Black people were dancing at a festival near Waycross and fired shotguns into them, killing two and wounding nine, one mortally. Reports say the men then tied the wounded and dead together.

episodes.title: Expulsion of Black pipe line workers from Sour Lake, Texas (February 1903)
episodes.summary: An unsigned note signed "WE" told Black employees on a Sour Lake pipe line to leave by noon, warning they would be driven away or killed. Twenty-five left for Beaumont. The contractor, John Kinsley, tried to get them back.

episodes.title: Lynching of J. D. Mayfield
episodes.summary: A mob going to take a Black prisoner from the Danville jail was met by a Black man who shot and killed a white member. Officers held him at the city building; the mob seized him, hanged him and burned the body. A sheriff's volley wounded five mob members. The mob then dynamited the jail, beat a second prisoner to death and attacked Black people in the streets.

episodes.title: Manhunt for the assailant of Florence Bruno and Annie Green
episodes.summary: Police and several hundred suburban residents scoured the countryside near St. Louis for a Black man said to have assaulted and mortally wounded two women; they declared he would be lynched or shot if found.

episodes.title: Lynching of an unidentified Black man near Alto, Texas
episodes.doubt: wire reported the lynching; the detailed report says the body had not been found
episodes.summary: A crowd of thirty took a Negro from a constable near Alto, Texas, after he was arrested for allegedly shooting into a house with women and children. Searching parties had not found the body by the next morning; the report is unconfirmed.

episodes.title: Stoning of the Lincoln School teachers' home, Meridian, Mississippi
episodes.doubt: principal's race not stated; attack on a Black school's teachers
episodes.summary: A mob of citizens of Meridian, Miss., attacked a school for colored children on Thursday, and the windows were smashed in. The paper says the attack grew out of President Roosevelt's attitude toward Booker T. Washington and other colored people.

episodes.title: Mob attack on Daniel Lewis
episodes.summary: A mob gathered and shouted "Lynch him!" after Daniel Lewis, a Black man described as heat-crazed, attacked two girls with a club. Detectives rescued Lewis and sent him to a hospital. No physical attack on Lewis by the mob is reported.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of John McCray
episodes.summary: A mob stormed the Peoria, Illinois jail intending to take the Black prisoner McRae, who had killed Detective Murphy, and lynch him. Sheriff and police held the mob off. McRae was later tried, convicted and sentenced to hang.

episodes.title: Keysville white cap notices (1903)
episodes.summary: White cap notices posted on two outbuildings near Keysville warned a colored woman to leave within ten days or be roughly handled. The notice said fifteen men were interested. Suspects were unknown.

episodes.title: Lynching of Jack Harris
episodes.summary: Fifty masked men demanded entry to the Clarendon jail, then took Jack Harris, a Black man held in a barn under a deputy's guard, and hanged him at about 1 a.m. after he allegedly assaulted a white farmer.

episodes.title: Killing of Tom Irvin
episodes.summary: Sheriff Walton deputized a posse that came upon Tom Irvin, a Black man, barricaded in Oliver Canada's house after he had shot a Mexican; the posse killed him before he would surrender.

episodes.title: Sixth and Vine street attack, Cincinnati (1903)
episodes.summary: At Cincinnati a riot followed three negroes' alleged insult to two white women; John McCarthy, a white man, was stabbed three times, and police saved the Negroes from death. The attackers are not described.

episodes.title: Peonage of Will Waters
episodes.summary: Three young farmers, William Shy, Arthur Clawson and Robert Turner, caught a Negro who owed them a debt, whipped him and forced him to work for them. In federal court at Macon they pleaded guilty to holding him in involuntary servitude and were fined $1,500 each, suspended.

episodes.title: Whitecap death notice to Garfield Williams
episodes.summary: Garfield Williams, a Negro tenant of James Daniels, was posted a notice signed by the 'W. C. of I. and C.' ordering him out within five days or be killed. Notice placed on his doorstep, dated Sept. 7, 1903.

episodes.title: Henderson whitecapping shooting
episodes.summary: A party of white men went to the cabin of Bob Willis, a Black man, to whip him for an unstated offense. Willis fired on the mob, killing Charles Brown and badly wounding a man named Garrett. The mob fled and the sheriff took Willis into custody.

episodes.title: Lynching of Henry Johnson
episodes.summary: After a shooting in which a white man was killed and two white men and a Black woman were wounded, a white mob dragged a Black man from jail, though he was not responsible for the shooting, and lynched him in the town square. A posse pursued the man said to have started the fight.

episodes.title: Beating of a Pullman porter at Sterling, Georgia
episodes.summary: Two men, George H. Smith of Brunswick and a stranger, beat a Black railroad porter said to have insulted a woman passenger. Conductor Temple ordered him off the train at Sterling, denying his baggage and further travel.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of the Pembroke prisoners
episodes.doubt: AP reported pronounced threats; no crowd at the jail; local paper doubted danger
episodes.summary: Nine Black men held in jail for the murder of an unknown white man near Pembroke; it was openly asserted at the scene that a mob would take them from jail and lynch them. Judge Cook called a special grand jury term.

episodes.title: Killing of Raymond Sizer
episodes.summary: Seventeen-year-old white store clerk Clarence M. Brooks shot and killed Black man Raymond Sizer after Sizer would not address him as 'Mr.'; coroner's jury ruled self-defense.

episodes.title: Barbour County whitecapping (1903)
episodes.summary: Whitecaps were reported driving Negroes out of Barbour County, Alabama, and running off labor on three or more large plantations. The paper says the cause is unknown but attributes it to the Negroes' conduct.

episodes.title: 1903 whitecap attacks in Franklin and Amite counties, Mississippi
episodes.summary: Whitecappers in Amite and Franklin Counties were again shooting into the homes of Negro tenants to drive them from the counties. No victims are named.

episodes.title: Whitecap notices to Black residents of Robertson County, Texas
episodes.summary: Whitecaps warned the Negroes of Robertson County, Texas, to leave the country under threat of whipping, posting printed notices on trees throughout the country districts. Many were leaving.

episodes.title: Killing of Trinnell Ellis
episodes.summary: Marshal Tom Crawford organized a posse to raid a suspected gambling shack at Thunderbolt. As the Black men scattered, Julian Beckett shot Grinnell Ellis, who was advancing with a picket, and Ellis was killed. Three others were arrested.

episodes.title: Drowning of an unidentified Black man in the Kansas River at Armourdale
episodes.doubt: no one killed him; drowned jumping from a boat as the crowd called it back
episodes.summary: A crowd chased an unidentified Black man near Kansas City after he was caught allegedly assaulting a white woman. Unable to escape, he jumped from a rowboat into the Kansas river and drowned. No group killing is reported.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Fred Jackson
episodes.summary: After Henry Resnet was found burned to death in his hut at Oxford, an angry mob of woodchoppers threatened to lynch Fred Jackson, a Black man, and pursued him into the woods. He was released from jail and has not been seen since.

episodes.title: Attempted burning of the Richardson house in Clive, Iowa
episodes.summary: About two weeks before the Anderson bombing, an unidentified party tried unsuccessfully to burn the Clive house where Chas. Richardson formerly lived; the door was soaked with coal oil but neighbors put out the fire.

episodes.title: Lynching of Charles Evans
episodes.summary: A white mob in Norway, S.C., seized a Black man who had shot a white man, hanged him from a tree and riddled him with bullets, leaving the body up a day. Several other Black residents were then whipped as a warning. Armed Black residents gathered outside town until state militia arrived.

episodes.title: Expulsion of Black telephone workers from Madison County, North Carolina
episodes.summary: A body of armed men in Madison county drove out of the county a company of Negroes who were working for a telephone company. The date and state are not given in the text; the county is identified by the paper's reference to Senator Pritchard's home.

episodes.title: Pike County whitecapping campaign of 1903
episodes.summary: Whitecappers ordered Black employees of the Williams steam saw mill in Cross Roads Beat to leave, and they did. Notices gave five and ten days and threatened shooting and death; signed 'Negro Skinner'.

episodes.title: Mob attack on M. M. Wadkins
episodes.summary: Masked men surrounded the house of M. M. Wadkins, a Black tailor in Tampa, and shot him twice as he ran; he escaped into a white residence and onto its roof. The mob dispersed and police guarded him.

episodes.title: Expulsion of Black renters from the Tomberlin neighborhood, Lonoke County, Arkansas
episodes.summary: During the past week nightriders notified all Negro renters on lands in the Tomberlin neighborhood, Lonoke county, to leave at once. Thirty-five families moved away. The paper links it to rent increases.

episodes.title: Warnings against Black mail carriers in Jackson and Lincoln County, Mississippi
episodes.summary: White people served notice on the Jackson, Miss., postmaster that employment of Negro carriers on the star mail routes must be discontinued, part of a crusade against Negro federal officeholders.

episodes.title: Charley Hudson peonage case
episodes.summary: Charley Hudson was held as a peon on Marshall Dill's farm in Lamar County, forced to cut railroad ties and confined in a windowless cotton house. After an escape, Dill and Bob Stevenson caught him, tied him to a tree and whipped him, and his clothes and about $10 were taken. Federal peonage prosecution followed.

episodes.title: Killing of Sarah Nealy
episodes.doubt: date unknown; before the June 21 report (Apr. 15 is another case's indictment date)
episodes.summary: Sarah Nealy was held by helpers while Allen Turner whipped her with a buggy trace, then handcuffed and hung by the wrists from a tree limb for two hours; she was left unable to see. Witnesses signed affidavits to the federal grand jury.

episodes.title: Riverside Park attack (Indianapolis, 1903)
episodes.summary: A gang of white boys at Riverside Park in Indianapolis, on the Sunday before this issue, set out to 'make it warm' for Black boys; the editorial says the gang was bent on mischief but gives no specific act of force.

episodes.title: Mob shooting of Len Beauchamps
episodes.doubt: one wire story; dateline Sedalia, Mo. in one paper, Vidalia elsewhere
episodes.summary: A mob pursued a new victim, who escaped, and shot or badly hurt Beauchamps; the headline says a Negro was lynched and shot while the guilty man escaped. Mob leaders are said to hide for fear of prosecution if they caused Beauchamps's death.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of William Mason and Thomas DeMoss
episodes.summary: About 1,000 people gathered at the Topeka city prison around midnight intending to lynch two Black men accused of murdering Bert Tutcher. The sheriff moved the prisoners to Lawrence; police found about fifty armed Black men massed nearby. The report is cut off.

episodes.title: Yorktown, Indiana, mob pursuit of a Black man (1903)
episodes.summary: A mob of twenty-five 'best citizens' at Yorktown, six miles west of Muncie, pursued a Black man seen prowling suspiciously. He refused to halt, jumped into the river and swam across, escaping.

episodes.title: Lynching of Ransom O'Neal and Charles Tunstall
episodes.summary: Several men entered a county jail cell at Angleton, Texas, where Black prisoners were held, and shot Ransom O'Neal and Charles Tunstall to death. Other prisoners were warned to cover their heads; O'Neal's bedding caught fire and he lost an arm and a leg to burns.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Tom Manns, Ed Morris and Charles Sanders (February 1903)
episodes.summary: A mob from nearby communities planned to take three Black prisoners held for assaulting John Farrow. Several hundred men followed the prisoners to the depot, where officers held them back with pistols, and the prisoners were moved to Covington.

episodes.title: Expulsion of Black residents from Sour Lake, Texas
episodes.summary: After a brakeman was reported shot by a Black man, warning notices reading 'Nigger, don't let the sun go down on you' were posted in 25-30 places at Sour Lake. Over fifty Black residents fled, a restaurant employing Black workers was guarded by armed men, and hotel and restaurant proprietors were warned to discharge Black employees.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of James T. Quarles and Henry Williams
episodes.summary: Shortly after midnight a mob at Nampa, Idaho entered the county jail and reached the first steel cage of two Black prisoners, Quarles and Williams. It could not reach the inner cage; Marshal Lillard and Mayor Sutherland kept it off until the governor and sheriff arrived. The prisoners were taken to Boise.

episodes.title: Lynching of Cato Garrett
episodes.summary: Fifteen Warren County men entered an incoming passenger train, took Gato Garrett, 17, from Officer Paul, and hanged him to a bridge east of the railroad. No shots were fired.

episodes.title: Norfolk road house shooting
episodes.doubt: who fired the fatal shot not stated; raid, possibly routine
episodes.summary: County constables about to raid a dance at a road house near Norfolk, Va., exchanged over 150 shots with Negroes; one Negro was killed and two wounded, and twelve were arrested.

episodes.title: Lauderdale County whitecapping of 1903
episodes.summary: Whitecappers shot into Negro tenant houses and terrorized the colored population in parts of Lauderdale County. Citizens at a mass meeting in Ripley raised a subscription and authorized a $200 reward for the guilty parties.

episodes.title: Lynching of Arthur Stewart
episodes.summary: A mob at Pineapple killed Arthur Stewart, a Black man held in the town jail on an attempted murder charge, then set fire to the jail to destroy evidence. The fire spread in a high wind and destroyed eight stores, the postoffice and other property, about $35,000 loss.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Kay Woods
episodes.summary: A mob pursuing a fugitive Black man shouted "lynch him." Patrolman Dugan faced the crowd and threatened to shoot if they laid hands on the man. No killing or seizure is reported.

episodes.title: Expulsion of John Dixon from Fremont, Ohio
episodes.summary: On May 19-20, 1903, a mob stoned the home of Black worker John Dixon, who had not joined the Clauss shear works strike, and drove him out of Fremont, Ohio; his family took refuge in the jail.

episodes.title: Expulsion of George Brown from Salem, Nebraska
episodes.summary: After a meeting of citizens at Salem, Neb., Black man George Brown, who had rented a house and planned to move his family there, was compelled to leave town. The paper says Salem had never had a Black inhabitant.

episodes.title: Lock Street school race riot
episodes.doubt: one brief; may be a two-sided schoolyard fight
episodes.summary: At the Lock street public school in Cincinnati, about 500 white children and 150 colored children engaged in a race riot; some colored children were badly beaten and fled home in terror.

episodes.title: Averted lynching of Bill Slaton
episodes.summary: A posse of citizens captured Bill Slaton, a Black man, near the scene of his alleged assault on an eighteen-year-old girl near Lithia Springs. He confessed, and would have been lynched but for the protests of the girl's father, Isaac Strickland.

episodes.title: Lynching of Case Jones
episodes.summary: Case Jones, a Black man accused of assaulting 12-year-old Margaret Bruce, was caught at night, identified by her, and confessed. He was strung up at daylight and his body riddled with bullets. The article does not say who did it.

episodes.title: Nahunta swamp lynching
episodes.doubt: killing implied ('never came clear'), one source
episodes.summary: A Black man accused of attempting to assault Mrs. Pat Herb near Nahunta was tried before Justice Johns at Hickox and discharged for want of evidence. A posse then re-arrested him and carried him off to the swamp, where, the paper says, 'they gave him a new trial there and he never came clear.'

episodes.title: Eighth Avenue crowd pursuit of George Smith
episodes.summary: A crowd of white men pursued George Smith, a Black man said to have slashed Robert Russell on Eighth avenue. About 500 people tried to take him from Policeman Muthall, who locked him up without trouble.

episodes.title: Expulsion of Black workers from the Raton round house
episodes.summary: The day after Night Marshal John Jones was shot at Raton, white Santa Fe round-house workers declared that they or the Black workmen had to go, and drove the Black workers off with picks, shovels and similar weapons. No deaths are reported. The cited Albuquerque Citizen article is irrelevant and should be replaced by the Santa Fe New Mexican item.

episodes.title: New Bern State Guard chase of 1903
episodes.doubt: harm from a fall during the chase
episodes.summary: Some Second Regiment State Guard troops returning from Morehead City set upon a negro boy at Newbern and chased him until he broke a leg falling over an obstruction. Date is inferred as recent, not stated.

episodes.title: Lynching of Jim Carr
episodes.summary: A mob at Millview, Hancock County, Miss., took Jim Carr, a Black prisoner held for killing Deputy Marshal Cobb, from the marshal in the woods while he was being moved at night, and hanged him. An earlier attempt at the Saucier jail was prevented by the marshal.

episodes.title: Shooting of M. Carter
episodes.summary: A posse with bloodhounds tracked a Negro suspected of firing on white man M. V. Blum to the house of M. Carter two miles from Shelby. When the posse broke down the door, it fired and fatally wounded Carter, who had fired twice. He was brought to Shelby and said he would be lynched if he recovered.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Adam Stewart
episodes.summary: Adam Stewart, colored, who shot John Imler near Ridgely, was in danger of lynching by angry neighborhood residents and was removed to jail by the sheriff. Imler was operated on at City Hospital.

episodes.title: Whipping and expulsion of Black residents of Cooper, Texas
episodes.summary: Posted notices in Cooper County warned negroes to leave or face consequences. Three Black leaders were taken from their homes and flogged and forced out of the county, after three others were whipped a week earlier.

episodes.title: Attacks on Black Western Union messengers in Richmond, 1903
episodes.summary: During a Western Union messengers' strike over pay cuts and the hiring of Black replacements, strikers or sympathizers stabbed Black messenger James Randolph in the shoulder, and a party of boys drove another from his bicycle with bricks and smashed the bicycle. No arrests were made.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Lewis Hubbard
episodes.summary: After a Black man named Lewis Hubbard allegedly shot and killed constable Peter Heck in Ridgley, Illinois, posses and police searched for him. Villagers said he would be summarily dealt with if captured.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Doc Bacon
episodes.summary: A Chase City delegation gathered at the Boydton jail as the sheriff tried to move "Doc" Bacon, who was under a respite from hanging, and demanded he not be removed. Armed posse faced the crowd until Judge Holmes persuaded it to disperse and the prisoner was taken away.

episodes.title: Assault on John Logan
episodes.summary: Three unknown white men assaulted John Logan, a Black youth, on South Meridian street, beating him and puncturing his bicycle. Patrolmen Dolby and Gregory were investigated over the charge they had used him as a decoy against the 'bungaloo' rowdies.

episodes.title: Assault on Will Baker at Selma
episodes.summary: Five or six young white men on the Selma river bank robbed Will Baker, a Black man, after a craps game, struck him with a stick, threatened to cut his throat with a razor, and threw him into the river. Four men were arrested.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Leroy Gibbons
episodes.summary: After Dupree Holmes disappeared, Leroy Gibbons was arrested and his wife said he had killed Holmes with a hoe. A party taking him toward Keysville lost him; the headline says he was probably lynched.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Johnson Reed
episodes.summary: Late on a Sunday, groups gathered near the Pikeville county jail intending to hang Johnson Reed, a Black prisoner accused of assaulting Little Martha Hall. Officers deputized about three dozen guards, citizens urged abandonment, and the crowd dispersed.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching in Indianapolis (April 1903)
episodes.summary: Police turned in a general fire alarm to prevent a crowd of infuriated white men from lynching a Black man in Indianapolis. No physical attack on the man is reported.

episodes.title: Whipping of Ned Sparkman
episodes.doubt: one dispatch says the masked men were 'supposed to have been negroes'
episodes.summary: Masked men whipped Negro preacher Ned Sparkman near Bethune, fired several shots into his house, wounding him in the face, and told him to leave the community. The paper says the crowd was supposed to have been negroes.

episodes.title: Whipping of Black brakemen at Lufkin, Texas
episodes.summary: A mob in Lufkin, Texas took two Black brakemen of the Houston, East and West Texas Railroad from a caboose, whipped them severely, and then fired several shots into the car, just missing the conductor. Citizens later condemned the mob and offered a reward.

episodes.title: Dynamiting of the James store at Beggs, Indian Territory
episodes.summary: Two store buildings at Beggs were destroyed by dynamite, and posters showing a Negro hanging from a telegraph pole appeared for three nights after the James family, Black newcomers, opened a store. Officials feared race trouble. The text breaks off before the poster's inscription.

episodes.title: White Hall sawmill whitecapping
episodes.summary: A band of white planters in Poynsett County, Arkansas, threatened and forced Afro-American sawmill laborers to leave, causing the mill to suspend. A deputy marshal then arrested eleven white planters for whitecapping, at the mill owner's instigation.

episodes.title: Lynching of Minor Long
episodes.lists: None (not in Beck–Tolnay, Seguin–Rigby or HAL)
episodes.summary: Masked men went to the St. Francisville parish jail, took the jailer's keys, and fired a volley into the steel cage of Minor Long, a Negro prisoner, killing him. The men then dispersed.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of John Broadnax
episodes.doubt: threat rests on talk and rumors; a Reidsville report thought it mostly talk
episodes.summary: After Sydney Blair was killed in Carmel section, neighbors gathered at the house and talk of lynching arose; Deputy Sheriff Faucette warned them off and the suspect was taken to Greensboro. No attack on the prisoner is reported.

episodes.title: 1903 Smith County, Mississippi, mob killings and expulsion
episodes.doubt: killings meet the lynching definition; retyped as a community attack (massacre rule); B-T 4180
episodes.summary: A mob of white-described 'Christians' killed four Negro men and one woman and badly injured ten others at Forest, Miss., the first of the week, though none of the victims had been convicted of any crime. The attack followed a shooting of a white man from ambush.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of William Keys and Joe Tyler
episodes.summary: Open talk of lynching Black men William Keys and Joe Tyler, and a gang of 15 white men organized to tar and feather them and some white women. The two men were reportedly warned to leave town. No physical attack is reported.

episodes.title: Moultrie depot whipping
episodes.summary: After a Black railroad employee was released on bond for kicking a depot clerk, two white men walked him beyond the Moultrie city limits. He has not been seen since and is said to be unable to walk; a buggy trace was reportedly used.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Sherman Stevens
episodes.summary: A mob was organized to lynch Sharman Stevens, a Black man captured about two months before the trial, but officers took him to Opelika. At his trial, open threats were made that he would be lynched if not sentenced to death; he was convicted and sentenced to death.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Peter Gillette
episodes.summary: A crowd captured Peter Gillette, a Black man, at Whitehall after he allegedly assaulted a fifteen-year-old girl, and threatened lynching. Chief of Police Walker moved him by train to the Salem county jail, averting a lynching.

episodes.title: Montevideo courthouse crowd (1903)
episodes.doubt: threat only in the St. Paul account; Montevideo dispatches report no disturbance
episodes.summary: A threatening mob filled the Montevideo courthouse and streets while Joe Scott, a negro, pleaded guilty. It followed the sheriff's party to the train, which took him to St. Paul.

episodes.title: Enigma shooting into Black shanties
episodes.summary: Late at night unknown parties visited the still quarter at Enigma and fired into negro shanties, killing no one; the residents were badly frightened. The trouble grew out of a fight between a negro boy and a white boy.

episodes.title: Beating of Joseph White
episodes.summary: A family and neighbors at Newport chased Joseph White, a Black man said to have robbed them, caught him after a struggle, recovered the money and revolver, and gave him a heavy thrashing before releasing him.

episodes.title: West Liberty ball-ground riot
episodes.summary: A riot between Black gamblers and whites at a Beltzhoover ball game in West Liberty borough left Charles Kelly shot dead. Crowd beat Nelson Foster, dragged William Davis toward a tree with a rope on his neck, and was halted by a former police inspector. Garrett, Davis and Foster were left dying.

episodes.title: Attack on Joe Williams and Earnest Griffin
episodes.summary: On the night of Aug. 12, 1903, a white mob shot Black miner Joe Williams and beat Earnest Griffin into insensibility near Virginia City, Ala., during the miners' strike.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Charles Bynum
episodes.summary: Justice Morris of Driver, Va., held court at 3 a.m. by firelight to save Charles Bynum, a Negro accused of burning John L. Bond's barn, from lynching. The fire destroyed horses, vehicles, implements and cotton.

episodes.title: Sour Lake expulsion notices
episodes.doubt: two reports blame a practical joker
episodes.summary: Written notices posted at several conspicuous places in Sour Lake commanded Negroes to leave. Many Negro residents left carrying their belongings, and they appealed to white friends for protection. Whites bought many firearms.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Alfred Daniels
episodes.summary: A large crowd of excited persons gathered at the Jones County jail at Trenton, NC, and made threats of lynching against Alfred Daniels, a Negro held for the killing of Farnifold G. Simmons. Senator Simmons appealed for restraint; no physical move is reported.

episodes.title: Flogging of John Brown
episodes.summary: A posse of leading citizens captured Negro John Brown near Fort Madison, tied him with ropes and chains to a trestle, and flogged him, and the crowd freed him after he promised never to return to South Carolina.

episodes.title: Lynching of John Thomas
episodes.summary: After a Black man shot and killed a sheriff in St. Charles Parish, all the white men went after him, shot him to death, dragged the body three miles, then broke into his house and burned his furniture and belongings with the body in the colored church yard.

episodes.title: Tenderloin mob threat against John Brown (1903)
episodes.doubt: one account describes a rush on the police (attempted)
episodes.summary: A Black cabman, John Brown, stabbed white cabman Michael Lynch in a fight in the Tenderloin. Patrolman Ruseelier clubbed Brown to make him release Lynch. A crowd of about two hundred shouted 'Lynch the nigger!' until police dispersed it.

episodes.title: Expulsion of Black residents from Scott and Smith counties, Mississippi
episodes.summary: Race riots in Scott County, Mississippi: white residents whipped occupants of numerous Negro cabins, burned their homes and drove the victims from the State. Negroes fled, leaving crops unharvested.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of William Hardy
episodes.summary: A marshal and posse entered William Hardy's Baconton house to arrest him for beating his wife. Hardy shot Raymond Mullins, a posse member, who was mortally wounded. Posse gunfire wounded Hardy, who was captured as a mob began organizing and was taken to Albany jail.

episodes.title: Clive whitecap attacks
episodes.summary: Unidentified parties dynamited part of I. J. Anderson's house in Clive, a village five miles west of Des Moines, the same night they posted a card ordering all Negroes to leave and sent unsigned letters urging employers not to hire them. Unsuccessful dynamiting attempt; partly destroyed house.

episodes.title: Whitecapping of Robinson's farm near Johnson Station
episodes.summary: A squad of white cappers visited the farm of Black landowner Robinson, two miles west of Johnson Station on the Lincoln-Pike line, one night recently. They tore down his fences, beat out his open cotton, scattered picked cotton and pulled and partly destroyed his corn.

episodes.title: Stanaford City killings
episodes.summary: Federal writ posses under Deputy Marshal Cunningham and Sheriff Cook surrounded Stanford City, WV, and fired on a house occupied by Stonewall Jackson, a negro, and other men in the mine workers' dispute; two or three inmates were killed and several injured, with 1,500 to 2,000 shots fired in the town.

episodes.title: Lynching of Jake Hines
episodes.summary: Jake Haines, a Negro, was brutally flogged to death in Colleton County, S.C., a few days before the issue, on mere suspicion of stealing. The paper says no attempt was made to fasten the crime on him. The number of attackers is not stated.

episodes.title: Killing of George Vann
episodes.summary: At New Bern, NC, officer C. Lupton arrested George Vann, colored, on an excursion train on a warrant from a quarrel. Vann allegedly grabbed the officer; five shots were fired and Vann died. Officer J. B. Dixon was shot through the thigh.

episodes.title: Expulsion of Black strangers from Vincennes, Indiana
episodes.summary: Vincennes police were ordering all strange Negroes out of the city after the Evansville race war. The order was reported alongside the arrest of Henry Thomas for alleged impudence to a white commissioner.

episodes.title: Attacks on Black sailors at Bar Harbor
episodes.summary: White sailors from seven warships at Bar Harbor fought Black sailors in the streets after a Saturday night ashore. Several whites drove Black sailors out of the YMCA tent where they had sought lodging, and two were knocked down on Main Street.

episodes.title: Caruthersville jail whipping
episodes.summary: A posse of citizens at Caruthersville, Mo., took three men and one woman, accused of pilfering during the flood, from jail on Saturday night and whipped them with leather thongs. The race of the victims is not stated.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Solomon Glasgow and Charles Strickland
episodes.summary: A mob attempted to lynch two condemned Negro prisoners at Holly Springs, Miss. The mob forced the sheriff's son to surrender the jail keys and searched the sheriff's home. The sheriff had already spirited the prisoners away.

episodes.title: Killing of Herbert Clifton and manhunt for George Jenkins
episodes.summary: A Negro, George Jenkins, is said to have shot and killed farmer Herbert Clifton at Banks, Tunica County, Mississippi. Large posses hunted him and a lynching was expected on capture; the hunt is reported, not a completed lynching.

episodes.title: Lynching of Jesse Franklin and Jim Phillips
episodes.lists: None (not in Beck–Tolnay, Seguin–Rigby or HAL)
episodes.summary: Two inoffensive Black men were taken from their homes by a band of white men in Rusk County, stripped, tied to trees and whipped. One died the following Saturday night and the other was critically hurt. Four white men were arrested, and the order went out that all Black residents must leave the county.

episodes.title: Booker murders and attempted lynching at Winchester, Tennessee
episodes.doubt: accused called 'Three Negroes' in one headline only; the Bookers' race never stated
episodes.summary: Simon Booker and his wife were murdered and their mountain cabin burned in Franklin County, Tenn. The paper says the "wildcatter distillers" accused them of betraying them to officers. Race is not stated.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of John Clements
episodes.summary: After Black man John Clements shot George Hobough at West Point, an armed citizens' posse was sent out in every direction to hunt him. Two men caught him near the railway and arrested him. Infuriated citizens were said to have threatened summary justice, which was averted.

episodes.title: Radford Fair Grounds lynching threat
episodes.summary: After a Black man struck a white man with a whip at the Radford Fair Grounds, an angry crowd cried lynch him. Joseph R. Jordan quelled the crowd and Sergeant McNeal took the man to jail; no physical attack is reported.

episodes.title: Lynching of Walter Davis
episodes.summary: A mob of several hundred men broke through the city jail wall with a telephone pole and sledgehammers, took Negro prisoner Walter Davis, and hanged him to a tree in Marshall. The lynching followed the ambush killing of Constable Hayes that morning.

episodes.title: Beating of Daniel Allen at the Seamen's Union
episodes.summary: On Tuesday in the Seamen's Union West street branch, the shipping agent and several white members beat Black seaman Daniel Allen over a shipwreck fee claim. Black members came upstairs, the whites fled, and no arrests were made.

episodes.title: Texarkana pest house whitecap raid
episodes.summary: An editorial praises Texarkana for organizing to defend a lone Black man in the pest house against whitecappers. The attack is only named in passing; no act is described.

episodes.title: Lynching of John Fogle
episodes.summary: Citizens from nearby towns searched for a Negro accused of attempted assault on a young white woman at Rose's. Tracked with bloodhounds to his cabin before dawn, he was identified by the woman, taken to a swamp, strung up and riddled with bullets.

episodes.title: Whitecapping and Black flight from Amite County, Mississippi
episodes.summary: A brief reports that many Negroes are leaving Mississippi in Amite county despite a compromise agreement. The brief gives no cause, attackers or acts of force.

episodes.title: Sulphur Springs whippings (1903)
episodes.summary: A party of whites publicly whipped a Black school teacher said to have insulted a young white woman, then whipped several Black men who protested. The crowd warned the men to go to work quickly or leave town.

episodes.title: Red Bank lynching threat (1903)
episodes.summary: About fifty people gathered at the Red Bank lockup after a Black man was accused of assaulting the mayor's daughter. A businessman said there would be a lynching unless he was removed from town by night. Police hurried him to the Freehold county jail; no attack on the lockup was reported.

episodes.title: Posse attack on Hal Smith's house, Amherst County, Virginia
episodes.summary: An armed white posse led by a man named Martin went to the house of Hal Smith, an elderly Black man, 'for a little fun'. Smith, his two sons and a nephew fired back and about eight posse members were wounded. The date is only 'the other day' before 1903-01-24; a possible link to the Smiths jailed for wounding Thomas J. Carter is inferred from name and county.

episodes.title: Lynching of Mitchell Gilbert
episodes.summary: The body of Mitchell Gilbert, colored, a former farm hand, was found hanging from a tree two miles south of Cordele on the Wenona road, riddled with bullets. The cause and perpetrators were not known; neighbors heard shots during the night and did not investigate.

episodes.title: Fremont riot (1903)
episodes.summary: A strike clash at the Clauss shear works in Fremont, Ohio, killed a striker and injured several others. Walter Stratton, Lorenzo Martin and Wheeler Kimbro, who the paper says were defending their lives from a mob, were jailed and indicted for murder. A second mob would have lynched them but for Sheriff Mason.

episodes.title: Bartlesville vigilance committee ultimatum (1903)
episodes.summary: White union men at Bartlesville, Indian Territory, angered at George Keeler's hiring of Black men to dig a cellar, organized a vigilance committee and gave the Black workers until that night to leave town. About two dozen made plans to go, many on foot for Kansas.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Dock Bacon and Anderson Finch
episodes.summary: Armed white men gathered near the Banner Warehouse at Chase City at 1 a.m. demanding summary action against negro prisoners accused of assaulting a white woman. Wise counsel prevented a lynching; the prisoners were moved to Boydton jail under guard.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Johnson at Kaufman, Texas
episodes.summary: A mob gathered at Kaufman, Texas, to lynch a colored man accused of a brutal assault on a white woman. Two white military companies were called out and the volunteers interposed, saving him.

episodes.title: Wrightsville lynching threat (1903)
episodes.summary: Citizens of Wrightsville planned to apprehend unknown Negroes said to chase white women at night and threatened lynch law if they succeeded.

episodes.title: Mount Vernon trolley strike and coercion of Black replacement workers
episodes.summary: Between 300 and 400 Italian members of the Dirt Diggers' union marched to a work site where sixty Negroes were working, persuaded them to quit and join the strike, and got practically all laborers in the city to quit. Police then guarded men at a contractor's sewer job.

episodes.title: Greenwood County church burning (1903)
episodes.summary: A Negro church was burned in the backwoods of Greenwood county, South Carolina, on the same night that three white men were shot and wounded. The perpetrators of the burning are not named, and the paper does not say the two events were connected.

episodes.title: Brightwood Y.M.C.A. mob threat
episodes.summary: A Black man who stabbed-in-fight and begged alms at the Brightwood Railroad Y.M.C.A. was stabbed several times, fled to a grocery store, and was followed by a howling mob threatening lynching on Saturday night; he boarded a street car and was not seen again.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Charles Lockett
episodes.summary: After a Black man, Charles Lockett, was held at Mrs. Susie Wells's home for an alleged attack, a large crowd gathered and made many lynching threats. Patrolmen took him away by a back street to the Tower.

episodes.title: Stoning of the Jas. Grimes house in Boone
episodes.summary: On the Thursday night before this issue, several men went to the home of Jas. Grimes, a Black resident on the edge of town, and pelted it with stones, breaking many windows and frightening the occupants. The paper calls the men 'gentlemen (?)'.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of David James
episodes.summary: An infuriated crowd of about 500 at Camden threatened to lynch David James, a Negro arrested for insulting a white woman, shouting "Lynch him!" while Constable Christman held him. The crowd pressed forward but was quieted by a game warden and a squire.

episodes.title: Lynching of Banjo Peavy
episodes.summary: After Banjo Peavy shot W. Cope Winslow, Jr., on his farm near Fort Valley, a posse captured him and turned him over to the sheriff. At 8:30 p.m. a mob overpowered the officer and guard, took Peavy to Branham's Grove, hanged him and fired about 300 bullets into the body.

episodes.title: Raleigh street car seat incident (1903)
episodes.summary: After a football game at the Fair Grounds, a gentleman and others seized two Black men who remained seated when white college girls boarded a street car, and pulled them from their seats. The paper says the rumor of a fight was untrue.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of John Black
episodes.summary: Black man John Black, arrested for poisoning his wife, was the subject of some lynching threats; he was brought to Kershaw and locked in the guard house before transfer to Camden jail. No physical move by a group is reported.

episodes.title: Beating of James Gale
episodes.summary: A mob of boys and young men severely beat James Gale, a colored man, at Fifth and King streets last night. He ran to the police station, where his injuries were dressed.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of William Bradway
episodes.summary: On Wednesday night a mob of about 300 gathered around officers' wagon carrying William Bradway, a colored prisoner, and tried to get hold of him, claiming they wanted to lynch him.

episodes.title: Kansas City Southern train riot (1903)
episodes.summary: In a fight on a Kansas City Southern train near Rosepine, Vernon Parish, Louisiana, one Negro and one white man were killed and four Negroes and one white man wounded. A white man shot the Negro prisoner who had overpowered a deputy sheriff; some forty shots were fired and train windows shot out.

episodes.title: Barney shooting and race-riot scare
episodes.summary: Citizens at Barney telephoned for Sheriff Conolly after a white man shot and killed a Black man and Black people took up the fight. The sheriff left Quitman with an armed posse on a special train; the paper expects no serious trouble.

episodes.title: Expulsion notice to the Dabney brothers at Port Royal, Virginia
episodes.summary: After a white physician was struck down at Port Royal, citizens, suspecting a Black man named Dabney and his brothers, gave them notice to leave Caroline County within twenty-four hours. The sheriff then sought them.

episodes.title: Lynching of William Williams
episodes.summary: A Black farm hand named Williams was caught about six hours after an alleged attempted criminal assault on a 7-year-old white girl and lynched about a mile from Whigham, Ga. Citizens were incensed and the affair was kept quiet.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of dining-car porters at Raton
episodes.summary: A mob of 75 to 100 men tried to break into the Raton county jail at night to seize five Black prisoners accused of killing Night Marshal John Jones. Sheriff refused entry; mob smashed the doors with sledges. The prisoners had already been spirited to Las Vegas.

episodes.title: Central Park incident in Henderson, Kentucky
episodes.summary: After a Black woman's remark to a white lady at Central Park, whites in Henderson, Ky., drove other Black people out of the park on a Sunday night in September 1903.

episodes.title: Warning to Black residents of Bloomfield, Indiana (1903)
episodes.summary: A letter from a self-described committee of Linton citizens to Charles Shelton, a Black Bloomfield resident, ordered all Black people to leave Greene County by July 25 or 'receive a visit.'

episodes.title: Assault on Roland Alston at the Columbian Institution for the Deaf and Dumb
episodes.summary: About fifty students at the Columbian Institution for the Deaf and Dumb rushed Roland Alston, a colored assistant janitor, over a note; they grabbed him, tore his shirt and threw him down until he broke away. He left his job.

episodes.title: Averted lynching of George Washington, Fayette County, Pennsylvania
episodes.summary: George Washington, a Black man, shot constable Isaac Hostetler on a Coal Lick train out of Uniontown. Officers arrested him and took him to jail, and a lynching was narrowly averted on the way.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Neely Zimmerman and George Williams
episodes.summary: A mob attempted to lynch Negroes Zimmerman and Burke, held in the Council Bluffs county jail on charges of robbing and attempting to assault two white women. Militia was called out, two leaders were arrested, and the crowd dispersed after Congressman Smith urged it to leave.

episodes.title: Lynching of Garfield McCoy, Wiley Anette and George McKinney
episodes.summary: A mob took three Negro men from the jail at Newton, Baker county, where they were held for killing a white man, F. S. Bullard. The mob overpowered the jailer, took the men a mile from town, hanged them to a tree and riddled them with bullets.

episodes.title: Reported lynching of Carrel Alexander
episodes.doubt: seizure rests on one hedged wire ('it is reported')
episodes.summary: After a Bohemian woman was reportedly assaulted by a Black man at Sealy, the man, Carrel Alexander, was identified and jailed. Officers took him away, and a mob reportedly got him. The paper does not say whether he was killed.

episodes.title: Lynching of Andy Clark
episodes.summary: Andy Clark, a Black man, was lynched at Leeper, Mo., on the night of January 21 for the shooting of white farmer James Herman after a quarrel over land. The paper gives no account of the mob.

episodes.title: Vineland street fight of 1903
episodes.summary: A street fight between whites and Black men in Vineland grew to a crowd of about 500. Black officer John Shockley fired at Tony Robinson, who knocked him down. A crowd chased Thomas, who was hit with a chair and escaped.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Joe Minor
episodes.summary: Laborers in a camp near Wellsville were indignant over the killing of Bennie Ganson, and threats of lynching Joe Minor, a Negro accused of the killing, were reported. Sheriff Wilson was to guard him on arrival.

episodes.title: Lynching of John Dennis
episodes.summary: A mob battered in the Greenville jail door with railroad iron, took Robert Denis, held after a preliminary hearing, and hanged him from a telephone cable before a crowd of more than 1,000. The ball game was delayed forty minutes so spectators could watch.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching at the McDonald colliery, Fayette County, West Virginia
episodes.summary: During a New River coal strike, guards tried to arrest a Black striker, who shot at them; a bullet killed guard William Mann. A crowd seized the striker and nearly lynched him before he was rescued and jailed.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Henry Washington and Cora Bolen
episodes.summary: After a six-year-old Black boy died, lynching threats were freely made against his father and sixteen-year-old sister-in-law, who were jailed without bail. The crowd lacked a leader and no attack is reported.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Lloyd Boyd
episodes.summary: Sailors and marines from the Naval Academy at Annapolis tried to lynch Lloyd Boyd, a Black man held for killing J. S. Kerns, scaling academy walls to reach the jail and threatening it with dynamite. Officers spirited Boyd to Baltimore at midnight.

episodes.title: Lynching of Henry Thomas
episodes.summary: Henry Thomas, a Black man, was captured several miles from Parish, brought back and hanged to a tree by citizens on Sunday night, 8 March 1903, for an alleged assault on a 10-year-old girl. He was found dangling the next morning.

episodes.title: Mob attack on William Jackson in the Tenderloin, New York
episodes.summary: White boys roped and surrounded passing Black men in Tenderloin district. When William Jackson intervened for an old man, a crowd of up to fifty struck, kicked and chased him, shouting 'lynch him' until Detective Quinn intervened. Charles Staub was arrested.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Dan Hinds
episodes.summary: Young men employed at Melish's button factory caught Dan Hinds, a colored youth of 18, and put a rope around his neck for an alleged attempted assault on a white girl. The sheriff secured him and held him for the grand jury.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Sam Bailey
episodes.summary: Officer Lark Strong tried to arrest Sam Bailey, a Black furnace worker, for carrying a concealed weapon; Bailey shot at him and struck him with a gun. Deputy Sheriff Coles raised an armed crowd that advanced on Bailey's house and pursued him, firing, but he escaped.

episodes.title: Whipping of Lorenzo Williams
episodes.summary: Phillips boys secured a buggy to take a Black man, Williams, and thrash him, which the paper says the community felt he deserved. The Evans brothers protested and were warned away.

episodes.title: Dothan buggy attack
episodes.summary: A mob of whites attacked several colored men out riding in Dothan one Sunday a few weeks before the letter. They broke down their buggy, drew pistols and dared them to speak about it.

episodes.title: Demands for the resignation of Black railway mail clerks (1903)
episodes.summary: Dispatches report that three Black railway mail clerks on the Alabama and Vicksburg railroad were warned to ask the department for another route; estimated 200 Black railway mail clerks may be affected. The warners are not identified.

episodes.title: Holdenville hotel dynamiting
episodes.summary: On Saturday night, the habitation of the Hotel Scott and one or two domestic workers were dynamited at Holdenville, breaking many windows. Dire threats had been made against Negroes and their employers; the colored workers left town.

episodes.title: Burning of Squire Williams's house at Johnston Station
episodes.summary: White caps burned the house of Squire Williams, a Black man two miles west of Johnston Station, after an earlier posted notice ordered him to leave. They then fired guns on the premises of Sam Caruth, intimidating his Black tenants. Sheriff and deputy were investigating.

episodes.title: Mob pursuit of William Daniels
episodes.doubt: 'Sparks' is the shooting victim's surname, not a place; place near Warfield on the Tug Fork
episodes.summary: A mob formed at Sparks to deal out summary justice to a Negro, who escaped by a circuitous route to Williamson, W. Va., and asked protection from mob violence.

episodes.title: Killing of Louis Hogan
episodes.summary: A clash between a Black crowd going to a musical entertainment and white men on Oxon Hill road turned into a rock-throwing fight. Louis Hogan, a Black youth, was killed, apparently stamped on after falling in a ditch. Three white men were held by a coroner's jury.

episodes.title: Expulsion of Black section hands near Corsicana, Texas
episodes.summary: Negroes working on the section in the neighborhood near Angus, south of Corsicana, were ordered to leave a short time before August 28, 1903. The article does not say by whom.

episodes.title: Whitecapping of Joe Shively and the Stevens women
episodes.summary: At 1 a.m. on April 26, thirty-eight unmasked men broke into a house on East Ninth street in Bloomington, Indiana, and whipped Joseph Shively, a Black man, with barbed wire and struck him in the eye with brass knuckles. They also whipped the two white Stephens girls.

episodes.title: Biltmore militia blanket-tossing
episodes.summary: Soldiers of the First Regiment, N.C. N.G., at Biltmore blanket-tossed several Negroes, chased Negroes off Southern Railway yards, and threatened to throw an old man into the Swannanoa River. The episode followed the regiment's resolution that no Negroes should remain in the neighborhood.

episodes.title: Assault on Robert Hamlin
episodes.summary: Striking Teamsters James O'Brien and Robert Nelligan assaulted Robert Hamlin, a non-union Black coal wagon driver, at Washington and Dey streets on Sept. 7. Convicted of second-degree assault, they were sentenced to nine months in the penitentiary.

episodes.title: Assault on Joe Hallier and B. L. Greer
episodes.summary: Five men at pistol point marched UMW organizer Joe Hallier and Black union vice president B. L. Greer down the railroad track at Horse Creek, forced indignities, beat Greer severely and fired on Hallier, who was wounded in the arm.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Shack Johnson
episodes.summary: After Shack Johnson, a Black man accused of attacking night watchman Capt. James H. Haymaker, was captured, an infuriated mob pressed a revolver to his breast and beat him, opening his scalp, intending to kill him. An officer prevented the shooting and he reached a cell.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Major Lee
episodes.summary: A lynching bee was arranged for a Black prisoner, Major Lee, held in the Moultrie jail on a charge of attempted assault. Sheriff Murphy moved him by train to Thomasville. No mob action against him is reported.

episodes.title: Daytona peninsula manhunt and lynching threats (1903)
episodes.summary: On Sunday 26 April 1903 (inferred from 'last Sunday' in a 2 May editorial), a white woman fled a Black cyclist who stopped on a peninsula road near Daytona. The sheriff, city marshal and a crowd hunted for him and open lynching threats were heard. He was not found and one suspect was released. The stage should be threatened or attempted mob action with no victim.

episodes.title: Hahira near-riot of 1903
episodes.summary: A crowd of white men at Hahira fell into a dispute with some Negroes on Christmas Eve, reportedly over a killed turkey. The sheriff requested troops to prevent race trouble, and the crowd dispersed once the request was known. No violence is reported.

episodes.title: Whitecap attack on Lucius Brownlee
episodes.summary: Several nights before July 27, whitecaps called Monroe County Black man Lucius Brownlee from his bed and fired a volley of bullets and buckshot at him, then left a note ordering him to leave the county. Four men were charged and bonded.

episodes.title: Lowrysville lynching threat of 1903
episodes.summary: The paper says Jim Gilmore 'barely escaped being lynched' at Lowryville about one month before June 1903. No details of the group or action are given.

episodes.title: Monroe excursion blockade (1903)
episodes.summary: Farmers in the vicinity of Monroe, Louisiana, had a posse with shotguns at the train to keep Black workers from leaving for Pine Bluff; the guns were reportedly brought into play. Planters were short of labor.

episodes.title: Expulsion of Black residents from Dearborn County, Indiana
episodes.summary: After a girl was murdered near Guilford, a huge Black man was arrested. The paper says an excited crowd of farmers would lynch or burn him if guilt were established, and might attack the militia.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Harvey Williams
episodes.summary: Posses hunted Harvey Williams, a Negro coal miner, after he was accused of assaulting a 13-year-old girl. Officers found him near Pocahontas and jailed him at Bramwell. The jail was guarded, and a report said he would be lynched, with crowds gathering in the village.

episodes.title: Lynching of Cornelius Lee
episodes.summary: At Plaquemine, a crowd of Black men beat banker Andre Gourrier and two white passers-by; white men arrived, the crowd was dispersed, and a shot killed Black man Cornelius Lee the next morning.

episodes.title: Expulsion of the Bushfield families from Vernon, Indiana
episodes.summary: A mob marched to the four houses of the colored Bushfield families, ordered them to leave, and after they left set fire to the four houses. The mob was said to resent the light penalty given Leon Bushfield.

episodes.title: Assault on Mingo Hamilton
episodes.summary: A gang assaulted Mingo Hamilton, a Black man, on West Fifty-fifth street on Saturday night: one struck him with an ash can and another stabbed him. Charles Kiernan was arrested and held in bail. A reported race riot that day was not found.

episodes.title: Lynching of Frank Dupree
episodes.summary: Frank Dupee, a Black man accused of killing white sawmill carpenter J. M. Ditter, was overpowered while being taken by an officer to the jail near Forest Hill, hanged to a tree and his body shot full of bullets.

episodes.title: Nutbush township whipping (1903)
episodes.summary: About forty masked men terribly beat and whipped a Negro man in Nutbush township on a Thursday night in late July 1903. He had been charged with burning the Kimball stables, and it was thought he might not recover.

episodes.title: Jeanerette acid-attack manhunt
episodes.summary: After an acid attack on engineer Norther Provost, a posse of citizens and officers pursued the assailant, believed to be a Negro, with hounds. Two Black men were arrested and released; citizens reportedly vowed summary action if he was caught.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching in Henderson County, North Carolina (1903)
episodes.summary: Five or six white men in a party were on the point of lynching a Negro after a row over a swapped or proposed belt trade in Henderson county; Asheville gentlemen rescued him at the last moment.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of John Dixon
episodes.summary: A mob formed at Sparta, Hancock County, Georgia, to lynch John Dixon, a Black man arrested for attempted assault on a white girl. Officers spirited him to the Macon jail. No physical attack is reported.

episodes.title: Alexandria street assault of September 1903
episodes.summary: Two white men, for an unstated cause, tried to assault a colored man on the street Sunday evening; one struck at him, but he escaped. No arrests were made.

episodes.title: Lynching of Jennie Steer
episodes.summary: A mob lynched Jennie Steer, a Black woman, on the Beard plantation near Shreveport, Louisiana, after she was accused of poisoning a young white girl. She was pursued, dragged from a hay loft, hanged, and bullets were fired into her body.

episodes.title: Whipping of a Black witness at Fort Myers
episodes.summary: Deputy Sheriff George L. Battersby said several white citizens whipped a Negro at Fort Myers because he gave false testimony at the Bowman murder inquest at Punta Gorda. The whipping is described as recent, and no date is given.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Joseph Johnson
episodes.summary: A mob of nearly 300 Slavs and Poles in the quarry district north of Lemont chased Joseph Johnson, a half-witted Black man, after he entered a house. They beat him and fired at him after he fell from a tree; he escaped into the weeds.

episodes.title: Expulsion of Black residents from Dearborn County, Indiana
episodes.summary: White people of Dearborn County, Indiana, were chasing Black residents out of the county after a white woman was murdered by one of them. One hundred had been forced to leave and others were notified to go, per the Wilmington Messenger.

episodes.title: Killing of Robert Stroud
episodes.summary: A posse of fifteen men went to a cabin two miles west of Lake Village where Robert Stroud, a Negro, had shot Amanda O'Brien; when he showed himself he was fired on, ran, and was struck by five bullets. He was brought to jail and died during the night.

episodes.title: Barbour County whitecapping (1903)
episodes.summary: Five prominent citizens of Barbour County, Alabama, were held under $500 bond each on a charge of whitecapping before a United States commissioner at Troy. They were alleged to have intimidated Negroes. The article gives no dates or specific acts.

episodes.title: Whitecap whipping of Black women near Myers, Missouri
episodes.summary: Negroes who had been flogged at Fayette and ordered out found refuge at a Black man's home near Myers. Neighbors ordered them to leave, then went to whip them; the men escaped, the woman was captured, severely whipped and ordered to leave.

episodes.title: Whipping of Herman Morrison
episodes.doubt: boys' group whipping after a quarrel; racial motive implied at most
episodes.summary: Boys aged fourteen to fifteen tied Herman Morrison, a fifteen-year-old Black boy, to a bush and severely whipped him at Bedford, Ind. Mayor Smith fined each boy $10.50 and reprimanded them; Morrison and a white companion were later arrested and fined the same amount.

episodes.title: Lynching of George Jones
episodes.summary: A mob broke into the jail at Mayersville, Mississippi, and shot Black prisoner George Jones, who was charged with arson. The article says he was shot; it does not say he died.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Minnie Pearl
episodes.summary: A mob of 300 white persons sought the life of Minnie Pearl, a colored woman, after she beat a white boy. Police arrested her and took her to the station before the mob reached her house. The mob then tore down the house and threw the furniture into the river.

episodes.title: Lynching of Sam Adams
episodes.summary: A committee chosen by a Pass Christian, Miss., mass meeting ran down Sam Adams, accused of assaulting Mrs. Peter Labouisse, and hanged him from a tree. The coroner's jury endorsed the method, and the accused man's father was ordered out of the county.

episodes.title: Ninth Street riot (Wilmington, Delaware, 1903)
episodes.doubt: two-sided Ninth Street clash between an armed Black crowd and white men; Kramer's death laid by the inquest to a Black man
episodes.summary: After a night of violence in Wilmington, a gang of armed Negroes clashed with a party of white men on North Street near midnight. Shots were fired, Sergeant McDermott was grazed, a Negro was clubbed by police, and Creamer was shot, apparently fatally, by a Negro. Many arrests followed.

episodes.title: Macon lynch crowds after the killing of Thomas J. Conrad
episodes.summary: Crowds gathered at Macon to take a Black man, held by the Eastman sheriff after a train arrest, from officers and lynch him. He was not the wanted man, and no prisoner was brought back to Macon, so the crowd got no one.

episodes.title: Mulberry railroad workers shooting incident
episodes.doubt: one local paper, which calls the reports exaggerated
episodes.summary: When construction cars with Black workers were set out at Mulberry, the workers overran the town. Some citizens fired pistols to drive them back to their cars. The paper says reports of a wholesale slaughter were exaggerated and nearly fabricated.

episodes.title: Lynching of Tom Hall
episodes.summary: Twenty-five masked men overpowered jailer Taylor Dulworth at Wickliffe, Ballard County, took Tom Hall from jail and hanged him to a tree; the mob then dispersed. Hall had shot Crockett Childress at Kevil station the previous Sunday.

episodes.title: Flushing tunnel fight
episodes.summary: Marshal John G. Elliott was killed and William Smith shot in a tunnel battle at Flushing, Ohio, between officers and a mob described as negroes and foreigners. Three colored men were wounded, three captured, and three surrounded in a cabin by a posse, with lynching likely.

episodes.title: Lynching of Andrew Rainey
episodes.summary: A mob overtook Constable Bell and his prisoner Andrew Rainey, a Negro held on an arson charge, near Bainbridge, demanded him under threat of death, took him, and beat him so that his skull was fractured; he died the next morning.

episodes.title: Killing of Knowles by an Atlanta bailiff
episodes.summary: In Atlanta, a bailiff, J. F. Wood, with a money lender, went to a Black woman's home over a 90-cent debt and shot and killed her husband Knowles. Wood was acquitted of murder.

episodes.title: Killing of Lafayette Sims
episodes.summary: Police killed Lafayette Sims, a Black man who barricaded himself in a North Rampart street lodging house and shot at officers, after the fire department was called and preparations made to smoke him out. The dispute began when the landlord sent for a policeman who smashed the door.

episodes.title: Whipping of Ed Williams
episodes.summary: Augusta citizens took Ed Williams, colored, from the Augusta jail a few nights before and whipped him for impudence to young white ladies. He afterward left town.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Henry Holloway
episodes.summary: After Mrs. Tuton reported an assault by Henry Holloway, her husband organized a posse that searched for him. The sheriff found him first, hid him, and moved him to Goldsboro to prevent a lynching. He was later convicted and sentenced to hang.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Harry Bell and Fannie Shelby
episodes.summary: A crowd surrounded the Batavia jail and the Chicago Negro prisoners were spirited away to prevent a possible lynching. Earlier, a mob attacked City Marshal Kelly, left him unconscious and rescued the prisoners. Sheriff Burke's posse later arrested the pair.

episodes.title: Death of Will Davis
episodes.summary: Citizens ran down and shot to death Will Davis, a Black laborer at the Seaboard Air Line camp near Trussville, after he allegedly killed paymaster W. G. McCaa with an ax. McCaa's brother had wounded Davis as he fled.

episodes.title: Bridgeville mob attack
episodes.summary: A mob of whites armed with shotguns and revolvers surrounded Culver's store at Bridgeville, wrecked the interior, and fired on Joseph Andrews, a Black man who had stabbed white man Edward Smith; Andrews escaped and was pursued a mile. Several Black men who came to his aid were beaten.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Taylor Gibbs
