episodes.summary: Taylor Gibbs, a Negro, was arrested after an alleged attempted assault on Miss Mollie Hendren near Kirksville and brought to Lancaster, where an attempt to lynch him failed. Garrard county people were said to be incensed.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Oscar Franklin
episodes.summary: On the night of 27-28 June 1903 a crowd followed a policeman chasing Oscar Franklin, a Black waiter said to have stabbed a Chinese restaurant keeper's hand, and shouted 'Lynch him! String him up!' when he was found in a cellar on West Twenty-sixth Street. Policeman Beattie drove the crowd back and took Franklin to the station. No violence by the crowd is reported.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Frank Jordan
episodes.summary: Farmers searching for a man said to have robbed a house found him along Rancocas creek. After he resisted, a rifle ball shot off part of his ear. The crowd put a rope around his neck and threw it over a tree, nearly hanging him until he confessed. He was then jailed.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Will Roseboro
episodes.summary: Several hundred people from Cool Springs had watched trains to lynch Will Roseboro, accused of murdering Mrs. Dolph Beaver. When he was brought to Statesville jail on August 2, a small group of bystanders tried to take him from Sheriff Summers, who drew a pistol.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Ernest Blakeney
episodes.summary: A crowd gathered at J. H. Stewart's after a Black farm hand, Ernest Blakeney, entered his daughter's bedroom at night. Feeling ran high and many agreed he should be killed, but leading citizens persuaded the crowd to let the law act, and he was jailed.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Rufus Martin
episodes.doubt: one sentence: 'narrowly escaped lynching'; no details
episodes.summary: A Fort Worth jury returned a death verdict on Rufus Martin, a Black man accused of stabbing farmer Charles Schwackhanmer a week earlier. The paper says Martin narrowly escaped a lynching, with no details given.

episodes.title: Lynching of William Hopkins
episodes.lists: None (not in Beck–Tolnay, Seguin–Rigby or HAL)
episodes.summary: A mob at Whites Mill, Miller county, Georgia, took William Popkins, a Black man charged with assaulting his nine-year-old stepdaughter, from a train on which an officer was conveying him to jail, and shot him to death.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Cliff Weeden
episodes.doubt: one item; state not given (probably Georgia)
episodes.summary: Cliff Weeden, a 13-year-old Black boy, narrowly escaped being lynched at Canton on Monday evening for an alleged attempted assault on a 7-year-old white girl on Sunday afternoon.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Albert Going
episodes.summary: A mob gathered around the jail at Rome, Ga., where Albert Goying, a Black man accused of assaulting a white woman, was held, and threatened to take him. The sheriff heard a thousand men were gathering and had threatened to kill deputies. The governor sent militia to guard the jail.

episodes.title: Lynching of John Turner
episodes.summary: A mob broke into the Warren county jail shortly after midnight on Sunday, took out John Turner, a Negro arrested for attempted assault on a white woman, and hanged him from a limb in front of the courthouse. The coroner's inquest blamed unknown parties.

episodes.title: Killing of Bob Crouch
episodes.doubt: no paper says Sheriff Rhoden acted in his office
episodes.summary: Bob Crouch, colored, was shot on Main street in Saluda Saturday night and died soon after. A coroner's jury named Sheriff W. L. Rhoden and Matt Berry as the men who fired; Rhoden was taken into custody.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Ben Riley
episodes.doubt: 'lynching scarcely avoided' in one paper; no crowd action described
episodes.summary: Citizens were enraged after a Black day cook allegedly attempted to rape a white domestic at a Grafton boarding house, and a lynching was scarcely avoided. Riley was arrested, jailed and held for the grand jury.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Eugene Smith
episodes.summary: A crowd of about 1,000 gathered around a Liberty boarding house after Black porter Eugene Smith allegedly attacked a woman and her children. Crowd members struck Smith with clubs and cried 'Lynch him!' before citizens took him to jail.

episodes.title: Toombsboro curfew shooting
episodes.summary: Toombsboro marshal Rickerson and a posse exchanged roughly 100 shots with Negro men loitering after a curfew ordinance, Sunday night into Monday; no one was hit. Five Negroes were later arrested.

episodes.title: Assault on Charles Collins
episodes.summary: Two unknown white men assaulted Charles Collins, a colored porter at a Minneapolis saloon, and badly bruised him. His white wife prevented him from using a knife. The date is inferred from 'last night' in an article dated August 9.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of William Dorsey at Peach Bottom
episodes.summary: After a quarrel at John T. Moore's hotel, where Dorsey was shot, a mob was formed to lynch Dorsey and Haywood, two Black men. Legal authorities captured them and jailed them at York before any lynching.

episodes.title: Lynching of John Gilbert
episodes.summary: John Gilbert, a Black man bound over by a magistrate after being charged in the shooting of planter H. J. Hubert, was taken from officers near Pinckney Landing, Ark., by Hubert's neighbors and hanged to a tree. Hubert died the next afternoon.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of John Wilson
episodes.summary: After a Negro man allegedly assaulted a farmer's wife near Valparaiso, angry farmers and college students threatened all Sunday to break the jail and lynch him. No physical attack is reported.

episodes.title: Lynching of George White
episodes.summary: A mob lynched George White, a Black man, in Wilmington, Delaware, early on June 23, 1903, and burned him. Men had been invited in advance and told when and where to assemble; thousands witnessed it. Authorities were expected to consider arrests, but none are reported.

episodes.title: Killing of Will Smith
episodes.summary: A Black man hawking chickens in Memphis was arrested by Patrolman Boyles, who left him in Slaughter's store with a pistol and orders to kill him if he tried to escape. Slaughter shot him, and he died at City Hospital. The paper calls it murder.

episodes.title: Lonoke whitecapping shooting
episodes.summary: A crowd of white men shot into a camp of Black timber cutters in Lonoke County, killing Bob Armstrong, described as a harmless old man. Three local farmers were later arrested on a white-capping charge, and many Black laborers left the area.

episodes.title: Killing of Robert Good (John Goodwin)
episodes.summary: After a Black passenger, Robert Good, was said to have fired the shot that killed B. L. Wright on a train, a score of posses searched for him. Late in the afternoon they cornered him at McGehee and shot him to death while he resisted arrest.

episodes.title: Lynching of Henry Liste
episodes.summary: Whitecaps who had ordered Henry Lisle to leave and fired into his house two weeks earlier returned at night with armed horsemen and killed him at Green Grove, Lincoln County. Public sentiment is said to be strongly against the Whitecaps.

episodes.title: Cole City convict mine shooting
episodes.doubt: convict-guard shooting; two 'probably fatally wounded' per wire, none dead per Constitution
episodes.summary: Convicts refusing to leave a Georgia coal mine after a punishment dispute were fired on by guards; two were said to be fatally wounded and about 125 remained barricaded underground. Most of the convicts are described as Negroes, but the wounded men's race is not stated.

episodes.title: Beaumont refinery notices
episodes.summary: A notice posted at the Beaumont refineries told Negroes to leave the place at once or face 'skull and bones', with the added line 'You know what that means.' Found by men reporting to work in the South End.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Arthur Reese
episodes.summary: After Arthur Reese allegedly cut Pat Rowan in a Moundsville saloon, a large crowd in the Mayor's office shouted 'Lynch the nigger.' No attempt was made; Reese was jailed.

episodes.title: Shooting of Andrew Crawford
episodes.doubt: shooter contested; crowd present
episodes.summary: Constable Nolan pursued Crawford, a Black hotel porter who had drawn a pistol over unpaid wages, with Helmick and a crowd. Nolan felled him with his fist, and a stranger shot him through the body at an officer's order; Crawford was taken home in serious condition.

episodes.title: Attempted expulsion of W. M. Grayor from Paducah
episodes.summary: A number of people went out at night to escort the Black preacher W. M. Grayor from Paducah and warn him to stay away, but could not find him. He had paid his fine and was still in the city.

episodes.title: Stoning of the Masonic Temple on Courtland Street, Baltimore
episodes.summary: On a Wednesday morning between six and seven o'clock a mob smashed nearly every pane of glass and the door knob of a colored lodge temple and gathered bricks and stones. Earlier that night a white mob of about two hundred had stoned the building and pistol shots were fired at colored men.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of George Kenny
episodes.summary: A mob attacked George Kenny, a Black man found guilty of assaulting a 4-year-old white girl, at Palestine, Texas. Sheriff Henry Watts rescued him with great difficulty. The jury fixed his punishment at death.

episodes.title: Sixth and Broadway street fight, Paducah (1903)
episodes.doubt: weak: no weapons or injuries
episodes.summary: White people joined a fight between white and colored boys at Sixth and Broadway and took a hand against the Black boys and a Black cyclist, after which the Black people were hard to find. No injuries are reported.

episodes.title: Manchester Avenue police siege and killing of Elmer Chambliss
episodes.summary: Police held a two-hour siege of David W. Ellington's house after he fired at two men and wounded Patrolman Peter Dolan. Negro prisoner Elmer Chambliss, in police custody, was killed and died in an ambulance, shot through the back. A crowd threatened lynching until police quieted it.

episodes.title: Ste. Genevieve posse shooting
episodes.summary: A sheriff's posse in Ste. Genevieve County looked for Robert Bishop, wanted for shooting two people at an Oakville railroad camp. The Fair Play says a posse member shot a fleeing Black man in the head and body near Burke's camp; the Republic says he fired first and took four shots. He was captured and jailed, and the Fair Play says he was not Bishop.

episodes.title: Stroud restaurant dynamiting
episodes.summary: Monday night a stick of dynamite was exploded under a shack used by Black restaurateur James Watkins while Black patrons were inside, demolishing the floor and breaking windows. None were injured; several arrests were made and released.

episodes.title: Exclusion of Wallace circus's Black workers from Linton, Indiana
episodes.summary: Linton townspeople, mostly coal miners and families, gave notice that Black circus workers must not enter the town. Threats were strong; the Wallace company held the Black workers at Switz City and the show was given without them.

episodes.title: Lynching of George Kincaid
episodes.summary: A mob gathered at Ruleville on Saturday to lynch George Kincaid, a Black man accused of wounding two men years earlier. A deputy sheriff had him spirited away and handed over on a presented order; his body was later found hanging in the swamps near Cleveland, Miss.

episodes.title: Kevil depot fight and expulsion of Black residents
episodes.summary: A battle at Kevil, a railroad station near Paducah, broke out between Black people and white youths after Black people ordered whites off their part of the platform. A dozen shots were fired; Tom Hall was shot through the arm and a white man, Childress, was fatally shot.

episodes.title: Hanging of a Black man at Mer Rouge, Louisiana (1903)
episodes.doubt: single line; death not stated
episodes.summary: A Black man described as a bad negro who tried to run the town was strung up to a limb at Mer Rouge. The paper gives no date, actors or count of those involved, and does not say the man died.

episodes.title: Expulsion of Black hotel workers from Holdenville, Indian Territory (1903)
episodes.summary: Citizens of Holdenven, Indian Territory, enforcing a rule that "no negroes shall live here," dynamited the homes of colored people and made other demonstrations. Race excitement was reported in the town.

episodes.title: Mobbing of George Jerome and expulsion of Black men from Howell, Indiana
episodes.summary: A Black conductor hired by a street railway running from Evansville was taken off at Howells, Ind., and beaten by a gang of whites, who ordered him never to run a car there again. The mob then terrorized Black residents, driving three into hiding and apparently clearing the town of them.

episodes.title: Beating of Sanders at the Atlantic Coast Line shops, Wilmington
episodes.summary: At the Atlantic Coast Line shops in Wilmington, over two hundred workmen nearly mobbed and badly beat a Negro worker named Sanders at the noon hour after he cursed a workman. Some 500 Black workers then walked out. The railroad started an investigation.

episodes.title: Killing of 'Uncle A.' Finney
episodes.lists: None (not in Beck–Tolnay, Seguin–Rigby or HAL)
episodes.summary: White men, said to be Virginians, shot down an elderly Black ex-slave at the door of his log cabin in Franklin County, reportedly because they believed him a sorcerer. The killing was reported a few days before the article.

episodes.title: Gillsburg lynching and reported riot
episodes.lists: None (not in Beck–Tolnay, Seguin–Rigby or HAL)
episodes.doubt: riot toll of 18 from one unconfirmed dispatch; same night as the Kentwood wreck
episodes.summary: A posse of fifty or more hunted a Black man accused of assaulting a white woman overnight and hanged him from a tree behind a barn at Gillsburg on Sunday, November 15. He is not named. A single wire dispatch datelined Kentwood, La. (five reprints) adds that eighteen Black people were killed in a riot that followed; the figure is "reported here tonight", names no one, and is never confirmed, corrected, or reported by the Black press.

episodes.title: Orchard Park dynamiting
episodes.summary: Early on August 8, a mob of men and boys dynamited and set fire to a house being built in Orchard Park, Oklahoma City, for a Black woman named Warner. Whites had warned Black residents to leave, and they refused. A race war was feared.

episodes.title: Pell City mob attack
episodes.summary: A crowd of thirty or more white men pursued a Black man near the ball grounds after he threw a rock, then fired on his home, wounding him and a child. That night the mob burned a neighboring Black family's dwelling, leaving the family homeless.

episodes.title: Fort Riley maneuvers clash between Texas militia and Black cavalrymen
episodes.summary: During the army maneuvers at Fort Riley, Kansas, Texas soldiers, after a fight over a white servant boy and a Black soldier striking a Texan, threatened to clean up the Negroes and bar them from passing their camp. Black soldiers then beat some Texans.

episodes.title: Whipping of Will Sewell
episodes.summary: In April 1903 Will Sewell, a Negro farm hand, was tied and whipped with a wagon whip until blood ran and he could not work for three weeks. Evidence said it was given as medicine and tonic.

episodes.title: Wilmington City Hall mob (1903)
episodes.summary: A crowd at Market and King streets before Wilmington City Hall and the police station (about 1,000 by the one account; the earlier summary said 7,000) demanded prisoner Arthur Corwell. Thirty police held them back, and the crowd jeered every streetcar carrying a Black passenger. Corwell was released on bail.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of William Butler
episodes.summary: After a police chase and arrest of William Butler, an alleged murderer, an immense crowd of excited men tried to lynch him; the policeman turned his revolver on the crowd. The killing of Dean Evans by Butler is a crime by one person and is not coded.

episodes.title: Exclusion of Black horse handlers from the Elwood, Indiana, street fair
episodes.summary: Horsemen exhibiting at the Elwood fair who employed Negro caretakers were told by those employees that the Black workers dare not enter town, having been warned not to approach the place; local authorities said Elwood was greatly prejudiced against Negroes.

episodes.title: Waterloo "all-white city" report
episodes.summary: An announcement that negroes must quit Waterloo, Iowa, is named as the cause of Des Moines club women's denunciation of lynching and of towns urging Black residents to flee. The article gives no further facts about the order.

episodes.title: Barbourville posse fight (1903)
episodes.summary: Deputy sheriffs' posse fought a band of eight Black men from Clay County near Barbourville after they allegedly tried to rob stores. Twenty shots were fired and one Black man was dangerously wounded; the others escaped.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Willis Martin
episodes.summary: Masked men gathered in DeKalb on Saturday night with evident intention of snatching Martin Willis, a Black prisoner held after a cutting affray. Sheriff's special deputies guarded the jail and the crowd dispersed; the sheriff moved the prisoner to Macon.

episodes.title: Flogging of Charles Johnson
episodes.summary: Hutch Walton, who had paid the fine of Black prisoner Charles Johnson and taken him to his farm, led a posse that captured Johnson near Amory after a horse theft, flogged him and jailed him.

episodes.title: Killing of Robert E. Banks
episodes.summary: A gang of white boys and men threw stones at Robert E. Banks, 18, in New Orleans, then fired two shots as he ran. He was shot through the lung, walked a block, and died. Three white boys were arrested; Gus Drew later gave himself up claiming self defense.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Thomas Hargo
episodes.summary: About 500 citizens chased Black man Thomas Hargo several blocks, ran him down, produced a rope and threatened lynching; bystanders knocked him down and threw bricks until police arrived.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of John Revel
episodes.summary: An angry crowd tried to take John Revel, a young Black man, from police at Twenty-eighth street and Eighth avenue to hang him to a lamp-post. Police drew pistols and the crowd fell back; a few held on until told they would be shot.

episodes.title: Intimidation of John C. Allgood
episodes.summary: Armed masked men stopped Black rural carrier John C. Allgood near Gallatin, Tenn., and warned him and his colored sub-carrier not to continue in the service under penalty of death. The Post Office Department ordered an investigation and suspended the route.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Clifford Bell
episodes.summary: A mob of about a hundred men pursued Clifford Bell, a Black youth of about 20, through Indianapolis streets after he struck a white man with a brick, crying 'lynch him.' Policemen with drawn revolvers saved him.

episodes.title: Expulsion of Black residents from Jeanerette, Louisiana
episodes.summary: About 25-30 Black residents of Jeanerette were notified to leave town and most left, warned never to return. A crowd thoroughly searched the negro section, and a riot was feared. The paper says the crowd was orderly.

episodes.title: Minneapolis candy store assault
episodes.summary: Two white young men ordered Black men away from two white girls at a Minneapolis candy store; a colored man was severely beaten and a large crowd gathered and talked of chasing Black men. A second melee followed and police quelled both.

episodes.title: Sixth Street mob beating, Minneapolis (1903)
episodes.summary: After a saloon stabbing of a white man, a crowd pursued three Black men and captured two. Bystanders struck a captured man held by a policeman, cutting his scalp, until police intervened; he was the wrong man and was released.

episodes.title: Whitecap notice to remove telephones from Black homes at Osyka and Magnolia
episodes.summary: Whitecaps sent notice to the Cumberland Telephone Company managers at Osyka and Magnolia to take phones out of Negro houses; the manager refused and offered a reward.

episodes.title: Killing of Richard Dukes
episodes.summary: A party of Black and white men attacked the house of Cebe Dukes, near River Junction, intending to kill him. He fled and was shot in the shoulder. The mob then shot into his father Richard Dukes's house, killing him as he ran, and burned the house.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Ed and Rosa Hutcheson
episodes.summary: Ed and Rosa Hutchinson, Negroes, narrowly escaped a lynching at Stevenson a few days before their Scottsboro trial. The paper gives no details of the attempt. They were fined and sentenced for writing obscene letters.

episodes.title: Bronx asphalt workers incident (1903)
episodes.summary: About 300 Italian union men surrounded 26 Black men working for the Uvalde Asphalt Company at 175th Street and Grand Concourse, told them to stop work or face trouble, and frightened them off the job. Four Italians were arrested.

episodes.title: Killing of an alleged looter in the 1903 Topeka flood
episodes.summary: A St. Joseph, Missouri, rescue party returning from the Topeka flood reported that it shot and killed a Black man caught looting deserted houses. The seven-Negroes-shot-on-a-raft report attached to this record is an unconfirmed East St. Louis, Illinois rumor of June 10 and does not belong to Topeka. No names, inquest or follow-up were found.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Fletcher Hollis
episodes.summary: Two posses of about one hundred men each patrolled the Smyrna river banks and marshes from Clayton to Bombay Hook searching for Fletcher Hollis, a Black man who shot Constable Wright. Papers said the posses would not allow him to be taken alive and he would probably be shot if caught.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching at the Grayson County jail, Texas
episodes.doubt: undated; on or before 1903-04-24, may be earlier
episodes.summary: An armed mob of about a thousand Texans with shotguns and Winchesters marched on the Grayson County jail and demanded a Black prisoner accused of assaulting a woman. Sheriff Lee McAfee refused and the mob dispersed.

episodes.title: Shanghaiing of eight Black men from Savannah
episodes.doubt: crimping also took white men
episodes.summary: Harry Oleson and Jack Johnson were arrested at Savannah, Ga., charged with forcibly putting eight colored men aboard a Russian bark as sailors.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Adam Jackson
episodes.summary: An angry mob swung up Adam Jackson, a Black man of Charlotte, for alleged criminal assault on a white woman in Washington County, Tenn. The sheriff arrived before he died, and a sheriff's posse took him down; he was bound over and jailed.

episodes.title: Killing of Philip Johnson
episodes.doubt: enforcing a citizens' expulsion order; the judge's charge mentions two shot to death at Campti
episodes.summary: Two deputy sheriffs shot and killed Philip Johnson, a leader of the negro prophet Smith's Church of God, at Campti when he returned after being ordered out by citizens.

episodes.title: Killing of Mrs. John Gundy
episodes.summary: John Gundy, a Black man ordered out of Amarillo, Texas, refused to go; his house was fired into and his wife was killed.

episodes.title: Whipping of Charlie Stark
episodes.summary: A party tracked Charlie Stark, a Georgia Black man accused of night prowling at a Sharon-area home, to Turkey Hill. More than fifty armed men gathered, calls to lynch and burn him were heard, and a jury voted 3-7 against killing. He was whipped in the road and ordered never to return.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Melved H. Rosier
episodes.summary: A party of masked men attempted to lynch Melved H. Rosier, a fifteen-year-old colored boy held for attempted assault, at La Plata, Charles County, Md. The warden removed him from the jail, and he was kept in the woods overnight, then moved to safety Sunday.

episodes.title: Lynching of Manna Ponton
episodes.summary: A mob at Halifax, N.C., hanged a Black man to a tree and riddled his body with bullets after he confessed to assaulting and murdering Mary Jenkins, a 13-year-old white girl. The mob made no attempt at concealment and dispersed.

episodes.title: Lynching of Amos Randall, Dan Kennedy and Henry Golden
episodes.doubt: Amos Randall was white; two Black victims
episodes.summary: About 25 armed men raided Amos Randall's bar at Mulberry before daylight and fired about 200 shots, killing Randall and two Black guards, Don Kennedy and Henry Golding, after the two were taken from a justice's court and questioned about the killing of Barney Brown.

episodes.title: Killings of Ned Roberts and Elijah Anderson
episodes.summary: During the flood, a levee worker named Roberts, who demanded his pay and threatened to break the levee, was shot dead after several shots rang out. Elijah Anderson, a Black levee worker who refused to work, was killed by the guard. Place and date are not stated in the fragment.

episodes.title: Lynching of an unidentified man near Eastman, Georgia
episodes.summary: Posses scoured woods and swamp for Ed Claus after an alleged assault on a white woman. He was captured at Everett City, escaped, and several shots were fired at him without hitting. Paper predicts a posse lynching if he is caught; another Black man arrested was found to be the wrong man before a mob reached him.

episodes.title: Stoning of Jacob Clarkson
episodes.summary: Three youths at Fifth and Franklin streets yelled "Lynch the nigger" at Jacob Clarkson, colored, and hurled stones at him. Each was fined $5 and costs.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Charles Peters
episodes.summary: Rumors of a lynching of Charles Peters, a Black man accused of assaulting a white woman in Reno, led to street-corner gatherings and whispered talk of advancing on the jail. Officers moved him to the county jail; no attack was made.

episodes.title: Whipping of Henry Meredith
episodes.summary: A mob at Armstrong, Mo., broke down the jail door and severely whipped a young Negro who had recently committed numerous depredations. No date is given in the item.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Robert Bishop
episodes.doubt: attackers race not stated; one paper (Republic) reports the hanging attempt
episodes.summary: After Robert Bishop, a Black grader, was accused of shooting Sam Ellis and a woman called Black Ida at a railroad camp at Oakville on September 11, other graders (race not stated) tried to hang him and chased him a mile; he fled south. A Ste. Genevieve posse later shot a Black man taken for him who proved to be the wrong man (separate record lean_1903-09_r2:g38).
